# A Guide to Reducto r-1-mini: How it Compares to LiteParse and LlamaParse Fast for Bulk Document Parsing

Reducto r-1-mini is a fair choice for low-cost bulk document parsing. But if you’re primarily pulling text from documents, start with **LiteParse**, LlamaIndex’s free, open-source parser. It reads PDFs and scans on your own infrastructure with no per-page fee.

For hosted parsing, **LlamaParse Fast** is an option at a price point comparable to r-1-mini. You can use Fast on its own or pair it with LiteParse to keep part of your workload local. Talk to us about pricing for your document volume.

## What is Reducto r-1-mini?

r-1-mini is Reducto’s lower-cost model for high-volume document parsing. The source positions it for simple documents and cost-sensitive bulk workloads. For complex documents with charts or intricate formatting, evaluate the output on representative pages before choosing a configuration.

## How much do r-1-mini, LiteParse and Fast cost?

| Reducto r-1-mini | LiteParse | LlamaParse Fast |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$1 per 1,000 pages** at the standard hosted rate. | **Free and open source.** You cover the cost of running it. | **$1.25 per 1,000 pages on Pro.** Fast uses one credit per page. |

List pricing can vary, and vendors may discount credits at higher volumes. A list-price comparison may not reflect production pricing.

## What changes between r-1-mini and full r-1?

Reducto recommends r-1-mini for cost-sensitive bulk parsing. If you’re primarily pulling text from documents, **LiteParse** gives you a free, open-source alternative with no per-page fee. For hosted bulk parsing, **LlamaParse Fast** is the closer comparison to mini.

Full r-1 costs **$10 per 1,000 pages** in the source draft. Reducto recommends it when accuracy or response time matters most. For demanding documents such as financial filings with dense tables and multi-column layouts, compare full r-1 with **LlamaParse Agentic and Agentic Plus**.

## Is r-1-mini the right choice for production?

For text-heavy workloads, **LiteParse is our first choice**. It reads digital PDFs and scans locally with no per-page API fee. For hosted bulk parsing, **LlamaParse Fast** is close to mini in price and handles both PDFs and Excel workbooks.

| Capability | LiteParse | LlamaParse Fast | Reducto r-1-mini |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Text and scanned PDFs** | Reads text and runs OCR locally. Returns text with its position on the page. | Reads digital text, runs OCR on scans, and preserves text positions. | Reads text and scans, preserves reading order, and returns positions for each block. |
| **Tables in PDFs** | Uses the page layout to reconstruct straightforward tables in Markdown. | Returns detected tables as rows and cells. Best suited to straightforward tables. | Interprets tables in the context of the page, including merged cells and nested headers. |
| **Excel workbooks** | Uses LibreOffice to convert the workbook to PDF locally, then parses the rendered pages. | Reads the workbook directly and returns one result page per worksheet, at one credit per sheet. | Hosted mini doesn’t accept Excel files. Reducto’s hosted service requires full r-1 for workbooks. |

The public ParseBench task, scores and supporting example for Fast versus mini remain pending in the source. Results for full r-1 or other LlamaParse tiers do not establish mini-versus-Fast performance.

## Which LlamaParse option should you compare with mini?

| What you need | Where to start |
| --- | --- |
| Bulk text parsing without a per-page API fee | **LiteParse** for local text parsing and OCR. |
| Low-cost hosted parsing for PDFs and workbooks | **LlamaParse Fast** for text-heavy documents, straightforward tables and Excel inputs. |
| Table structure that carries across merged headers or page breaks | **LlamaParse Cost Effective** is the first tier we’d evaluate. |
| Higher accuracy on dense financial tables or complex layouts | **LlamaParse Agentic or Agentic Plus.** Compare them with full r-1 on the pages where a parsing error would change the answer. |

## Frequently asked questions

### Can LiteParse handle the whole workload?

Yes. If you need text, OCR and page positions, you can run the entire workload through LiteParse locally. Fast is available separately for hosted processing.

### When is it worth moving beyond Fast?

Start with Fast for straightforward tables. If a table has merged headers, lacks borders or continues onto the next page, LlamaIndex recommends Cost Effective or higher. A useful test is whether the parser keeps each value under the correct header from one page to the next.

## Get started

[Try LiteParse](https://www.llamaindex.ai/liteparse) · [Get started with LlamaParse](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/parse/getting_started/)

For related context, read [Reducto r-1 vs LlamaParse: Parsing Accuracy, Charts and Configuration](/agents/reducto-r-1-vs-llamaparse-parsing-accuracy-charts-and-configuration) and [Reducto vs LlamaParse and LlamaExtract Pricing: Quality per Accepted Document](/agents/reducto-vs-llamaparse-and-llamaextract-pricing-quality-per-accepted-document).

description: "LlamaExtract Agentic Plus leads Extend Operator on localized box-word grounding in the cited ExtractBench Pro snapshot."

# Extend vs LlamaExtract Citations: Localized Evidence and Page Grounding

LlamaExtract Agentic Plus leads Extend Operator on localized box-word grounding in the cited ExtractBench Pro snapshot. That is a specific advantage to investigate when reviewers must find the exact evidence behind a field. Extend’s higher page-grounding score is a separate strength; show both measures, then test the evidence needed for an actual acceptance decision.

*Published by LlamaIndex, which created ExtractBench and develops a tested product. This article interprets a published snapshot and proposes an evidence-review rubric; it does not report a new usability study.*

## What is the difference between page and box-word grounding?

Page grounding asks whether the supporting page is identified correctly. Box-word grounding evaluates a more specific relationship between the answer and its localized supporting content. In the pinned Pro results, Extend Operator scores 68.84 on page grounding versus 66.01 for Plus; Plus scores 60.39 on box-word grounding versus 57.75 for Operator. The grounding subset contains 81 documents within a 100-document synthetic suite evaluated under a 30-minute task policy. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard-pro.csv), [grounding methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/main/docs/extractbench-pro.md).

Page-level navigation may be enough for broad exploration. Field review can require a narrower location plus the context that explains it. Score those needs separately in the evaluation.

## Why can a correct page still be difficult to verify?

Imagine a hypothetical financial page with the amount “125.00” appearing in four places: a line-item price, a subtotal, a tax-related note and a prior-period comparison. An extractor returns 125.00 for the requested subtotal and links to the page.

The reviewer must identify which occurrence supports the subtotal and whether its label, period and table match the requested field.

A more precise region can reduce the search space, but a box around the number alone may still omit the label needed to interpret it. Evidence quality therefore involves both localization and enough context to establish the relationship.

This is a hypothetical illustration, not a measured error by Extend or LlamaIndex.

## What citation capabilities does Extend provide?

Extend supports citation configuration at different granularities, and its release history includes word-level and array-citation improvements. A fair comparison should use the relevant current configuration rather than claim that Extend lacks citations. [Extraction configuration](https://docs.extend.ai/extraction/configuration), [extraction version history](https://docs.extend.ai/model-versioning/extraction/extraction-performance).

Keep extraction citations separate from parser output features. A version-specific limitation in a table-cell output option does not prove that the extraction service cannot provide field evidence.

Also distinguish the citation returned by the API from the experience built around it. Coordinate handling, page rendering, zoom and highlighting can affect whether a reviewer can use otherwise valid evidence.

## How should an evidence rubric be designed?

Evaluate each required field along several dimensions:

| Dimension | Review question |
| --- | --- |
| Presence | Is supporting evidence returned? |
| Page correctness | Is the evidence on the correct page? |
| Localization | Does the region identify the relevant content? |
| Semantic support | Does that content actually support the field's meaning? |
| Context | Are labels, units and relationships available when needed? |
| Completeness | Are all necessary pieces present for multi-part answers? |

Record value correctness and evidence support in separate columns. That lets you distinguish a correct number with poor localization from a precise citation to the wrong table entry.

Define acceptable evidence for each field type. A scalar amount may need one region plus a label. A computed result may need several source values and an explanation of the calculation. A multi-page array may need evidence for individual items rather than one citation for the entire list.

## How do arrays create additional evidence problems?

Repeated rows contain similar values and labels, so a citation can land on a neighboring record while appearing plausible. Evaluate item-to-evidence alignment, not only whether every citation points somewhere inside the correct table.

Use a labeled fixture with repeated amounts, adjacent dates and similar descriptions. Ask reviewers to verify a specific row without relying on the order in which the model returned items. If ordering is not guaranteed, preserve a stable mapping between each output record and its supporting evidence.

Missing records need a separate check. Evidence for every returned item does not establish that all source items were extracted. Pair citation evaluation with completeness and record-count checks where the workflow requires them.

## How should reviewer effort be measured?

Use a small task-based study to find out whether the evidence changes review effort. Give reviewers the same source documents and fields, and define what constitutes successful verification.

Measure time to a correct decision, incorrect confirmations and requests for additional context. Randomize presentation order where practical and distinguish unfamiliar-interface learning from evidence quality.

Preserve qualitative observations. A reviewer may explain that a region is precise but omits the column heading, or that a page link is adequate on a simple form but cumbersome on a dense statement. Those observations help improve the interface and the evidence contract.

Until that study is run in the intended application, the benchmark supports a grounding comparison but no quantified reviewer-time saving.

## When does each approach fit?

LlamaExtract Agentic Plus’s higher box-word result provides the more specific reason to prioritize it where localized support matters. Extend’s higher page-grounding result remains relevant when locating the supporting page is the principal evidence requirement.

On a simple form, a page link may be sufficient. On a dense statement, test whether the returned region includes the row and heading a reviewer needs. The application interface belongs in that test alongside the API response.

## Give reviewers a repeated-value fixture

Prioritize LlamaExtract Agentic Plus when localized supporting evidence is central to the review decision, using the pinned box-word result as the supporting claim. Retain Extend’s page-grounding lead. Measure whether reviewers can verify the actual fields; the benchmark does not establish reviewer-time savings.

title: "Workload Identity Federation for Document AI APIs: Secure Keyless Access"
description: "Use workload identity federation to access document AI APIs without long-lived application secrets, while retaining deployment and audit controls."
published: "2026-11-16"
updated: "2026-11-16"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/"
---

# Workload Identity Federation for Document AI APIs: Secure Keyless Access

## Short answer

Workload identity federation lets an application exchange a trusted platform identity for short-lived credentials instead of storing a long-lived API key. It can reduce secret-management exposure for document AI pipelines, but it does not replace authorization, tenant isolation, audit logging or a sound data-residency design.

## Why document workflows need it

Document-processing jobs commonly run in CI systems, containers, serverless functions and scheduled batch workers. A static API key in an environment variable may be easy to start with, but it can spread across build logs, developer machines, deployment systems and incident-response scope.

With federation, a runtime identity—such as a workload in a cloud account or a CI job—presents a signed assertion to an identity provider. The receiving service verifies the issuer, audience and subject, then issues a narrowly scoped, short-lived credential. The application uses that credential for a defined job and obtains a new one when needed.

## What federation does and does not solve

| Federation can help with | Federation does not automatically solve |
| --- | --- |
| Removing stored long-lived application secrets | Which users or workloads are authorized for which documents |
| Limiting credential lifetime and scope | Encryption, retention or data-residency requirements |
| Improving auditability of workload access | Secure handling of outputs, logs and downloaded files |
| Revoking a trusted workload relationship | Validation of extracted business data |

## A practical design checklist

Define the exact workload identities that may call the API. Restrict the accepted issuer, audience, subject and repository or cloud-account attributes. Grant the smallest workable permissions, separate production from development identities, set short token lifetimes, and log the identity, request scope and destination for each run.

Also plan failure behavior. A batch processor should fail closed when token verification fails, avoid logging tokens or document contents, and have a clear path for rotating trust relationships. Test a compromised or misconfigured workload just as deliberately as the successful path.

## Deployment still matters

Keyless authentication answers how a workload proves its identity. It does not answer where documents are stored, where model inference runs or who can retrieve outputs. For highly constrained workloads, evaluate the authentication design alongside private deployment, network controls, storage policies and model-endpoint selection.

LlamaParse supports deployments in a customer AWS, Azure or Google Cloud account and on Kubernetes in a customer data center. [The deployment guide](https://www.llamaindex.ai/agents/llamaparse-deployment-options-managed-saas-aws-azure-gcp-and-on-premises.md) explains the choices. Confirm the current identity and authentication options with the product team before making a vendor-specific implementation claim.

## Evaluate the workflow, not the feature label

In a proof of concept, verify that no long-lived secret is present in source control, CI logs, container images or runtime configuration; that tokens cannot be replayed outside the intended audience; and that a job can access only the documents and outputs it needs. A secure document AI integration combines short-lived identity with least privilege, data controls and an auditable operating model.

# Datalab vs LlamaExtract for Long Documents: Accuracy Across Pages and Records

LlamaExtract Agentic has a substantial long-document advantage over the tested Datalab configuration on ExtractBench. For financial reports and contracts, that is a reason to test LlamaExtract first on values whose meaning depends on earlier headings, units and notes. Request-size limits and segmentation tools matter operationally, but they do not measure whether the resulting records are correct.

*Published by LlamaIndex. Product facts reflect research through October 28, 2026. Examples are hypothetical workflow cases, not measured vendor failures.*

## Where LlamaExtract performs better on ExtractBench

| Configuration | Value F1 | Long-document Value F1 | Word grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaExtract Agentic | 95.65 | 94.73 | 82.33 |
| LlamaExtract Agentic Plus | 96.17 | 94.65 | 83.25 |
| Datalab (Accurate + Balanced) | 85.70 | 42.04 | 2.02 |

On the long-document slice, Agentic scores 94.73 versus 42.04 for the tested Datalab pipeline, a 52.69-point difference. That slice is a reason to prioritize LlamaExtract for long-document evaluation, not a guarantee about every document length or a claim that Datalab’s current service cannot improve.

These are published results from the pinned ExtractBench snapshot at commit 7004e29, checked on November 4, 2026. The suite covers 370 documents and 4,869 pages. Value F1 measures extracted values; it is not a straight-through-processing rate. LlamaIndex publishes the benchmark and develops LlamaExtract, now documented within LlamaParse Extract. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv), [methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/docs/extractbench.md).

## Datalab’s request limits and segmentation tools

Datalab’s limits documentation identifies up to 7,000 pages per request and a separate 5,000-page concurrency limit. Its long-document guide describes page ranges and segmentation, including mapping printed page numbers to actual PDF indices. The first limit concerns request size; the second concerns pages in flight. [API limits](https://documentation.datalab.to/docs/common/limits), [long-document guidance](https://documentation.datalab.to/docs/recipes/structured-extraction/handling-long-documents).

Large-file support reduces the need for manual splitting. The remaining design work depends on the document: which sections can stand alone, and which need information from elsewhere?

A short contract with cross-references may need more careful segmentation than a 500-page archive of independent one-page records.

## When should a document be segmented?

Segmentation is helpful when a file contains distinct records or sections that can be processed independently. It can reduce irrelevant context and make failures easier to isolate.

It can also remove information needed to interpret a section. A table may continue onto the next page. A definition near the beginning may apply throughout a contract. A note at the end of a report may change the meaning of a number presented earlier.

For each proposed segment, record the context that must accompany it:

| Segment type | Potential dependency to preserve |
| --- | --- |
| Invoice in a packet | Supplier identity or shared cover information |
| Financial table | Units, period labels and continuation headers |
| Contract schedule | Definitions and clauses referenced elsewhere |
| Research appendix | Figure captions and methodological context |

A segment should be independently understandable for the assigned extraction task, or explicitly linked to the additional context it needs.

## Printed page numbers and PDF indices

Printed page numbers and PDF positions can differ because of cover pages, front matter, Roman numerals or inserted documents. A table of contents may refer to the printed numbering rather than the index expected by an API.

Consider a hypothetical annual report with a cover and four preliminary pages. The table of contents points to printed page 12, but that content is not necessarily at zero-based PDF index 11. Blindly using the printed number can route extraction to the wrong section.

Create and verify a page mapping before extracting by range. Keep both the human-facing page label and the machine-facing page index in the result. This helps reviewers locate evidence and prevents later transformations from confusing the two.

When a document packet combines multiple sources, preserve each source’s identity as well. “Page 12” is insufficient if the packet contains several documents with their own page 12.

## A multiplier left on the previous page

Imagine a hypothetical table that starts on one page with the heading “Amounts in thousands” and continues on the next page without repeating that heading. A value of 850 on the second page must remain associated with that multiplier.

The workflow also needs to preserve which entity and period the column describes. A visually plausible number can become a materially incorrect record if it is assigned to the wrong subsidiary or year.

For the continued table, retain:

- Value and unit or multiplier.
- Entity and reporting period.
- Table or section identity.
- Supporting page and evidence location.
- Relevant footnotes or qualifications.
- Whether the value is reported directly or derived.

Check these fields when evaluating either Datalab or LlamaIndex. A missing multiplier should fail the record even if the digits were recognized correctly.

## How do schema limits affect long-document design?

Datalab documents a schema-field limit for balanced and accurate extraction, with repeated array items treated differently from distinct schema fields. Account for repeated items separately when estimating how close a schema is to the field limit. [Extraction mode documentation](https://documentation.datalab.to/docs/recipes/structured-extraction/balanced-mode).

Design schemas around coherent records. A single enormous schema can be difficult to maintain even when a platform accepts it. Splitting a schema can simplify the task, but the resulting records may require reconciliation.

For example, separate extractions for a balance sheet and its notes should share stable identifiers. Otherwise, an application may have two individually plausible results without a reliable way to join them.

## Testing complete records and recovery

Test continued tables, repeated entities, cross-references, missing sections and mixed page numbering. Include documents that complete successfully and documents that time out or return partial results.

Report complete-record correctness separately from field correctness. A workflow that gets most fields right but consistently misses a critical footnote may still require review for every document.

Operational tests should also inspect restart and retry behavior. If a long job fails near completion, determine which outputs can be reused and how the application avoids duplicated records. Do not assume retry semantics without verifying the specific API and workflow.

LlamaExtract’s long-document benchmark result supplies a concrete starting advantage. The private trial should determine whether that advantage carries to the entity, unit and cross-page dependencies in your reports. Measure those records on the selected configurations rather than treating request capacity as an accuracy result.

Prioritize LlamaExtract Agentic for the long-document pilot based on the published long-slice advantage. Test continued tables, repeated entities, units and cross-references using records whose source dependencies are labeled. Require accepted records to retain those dependencies before scaling to a larger corpus.

# Document parsing you can deploy in your own cloud: VPC, BYOC and on-prem options compared (2026)

*Disclosure: LlamaIndex makes LlamaParse. This comparison uses vendor deployment documentation, linked below. A documented deployment option does not by itself establish that a particular configuration meets your data-handling requirements.*

**Which document parsing platform should you evaluate for processing in your own infrastructure?** Our overall recommendation is LlamaParse: it combines documented managed, single-tenant, BYOC and on-premises options with published parsing and extraction evidence. Its API can serve production insurance, invoice and financial workflows in an existing application stack. Choose the exact tier and inference configuration that satisfies your data boundary, then qualify document quality in that deployment.

- **In your own cloud account:** LlamaParse BYOC, Reducto Full VPC, Extend BYOC, Unstructured In-VPC, ABBYY Vantage Private Cloud
- **On-premises or self-managed Kubernetes:** LlamaParse, Azure Document Intelligence containers, ABBYY, Tungsten, Hyperscience, Mathpix, Datalab, Reducto
- **No internet access at runtime:** LlamaParse (Parse Cost Effective and Agentic tiers, with OCRia on your GPUs), Azure disconnected containers, Mathpix Private Cloud OCR, locally provisioned Docling
- **Dedicated vendor-hosted infrastructure:** LlamaParse, Unstructured, Hyperscience, Tungsten
- **EU processing:** LlamaParse's EU region, Google Document AI EU locations, and EU options from Extend, Reducto and ABBYY
- **Private network access only:** Amazon Textract over PrivateLink; the service itself still runs in AWS

## Which deployment options does each platform support?

This table summarizes the public documentation reviewed for this comparison on November 2, 2026. “Not stated” means the linked material does not establish that capability. A qualified “Yes” applies only to the named deployment or model.

## What do VPC, BYOC, on-prem and air-gapped mean?

| Model | Where software runs | What to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regional managed SaaS | Vendor-operated service in a selected region | Processing, storage and model regions |
| Single-tenant SaaS | Dedicated vendor-operated deployment | Which resources are dedicated and who can access them |
| Private endpoint to SaaS | Vendor service reached over private networking | Processing location remains a separate question |
| BYOC | Software deployed in your cloud account | Inference, telemetry, support access and update paths |
| On-prem | Infrastructure in your data center | Hardware requirements and external dependencies |
| Air-gapped | Environment without external network connectivity | Offline models, licenses, installation and updates |

Single tenancy describes isolation; BYOC describes account ownership. Neither term guarantees offline inference. For example, [Textract PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/vpc-interface-endpoints.html) gives your VPC a private path to Textract. The API remains an AWS-operated service.

## Which platforms can run in my own VPC?

LlamaParse BYOC, Reducto Full VPC, Extend BYOC, Unstructured In-VPC, ABBYY Vantage Private Cloud, Datalab, Mathpix, Hyperscience and Azure containers support customer-controlled infrastructure. Docling is a self-run alternative.

Define the boundary first: your account, region or provider network? Ask for the data flow across storage, parsing, inference and logs. A parser in your cluster can still send content to an external model. Google service perimeters and Textract private endpoints do not establish account-local processing.

## Which platforms can run on-premises?

Azure containers, ABBYY, Tungsten, Hyperscience, Mathpix, Datalab, Reducto, LlamaParse and Docling document on-premises or self-managed Kubernetes options. Confirm the exact model and release: local deployment may not include every hosted feature. Establish hardware requirements, model distribution, upgrade ownership and incident support before selecting a platform.

## Which platforms work without internet access?

[Azure disconnected containers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/document-intelligence/containers/disconnected) document an approval process, commitment plan and local license file. [Mathpix Private Cloud OCR](https://mathpix.com/private-cloud-ocr) documents air-gapped operation. Datalab and Hyperscience state offline deployment support; establish how images, weights, licenses and updates enter the environment. Docling supports local execution suitable for air-gapped environments once required models and dependencies are present.

Extend explicitly says it does not currently offer fully air-gapped deployment. LlamaParse supports air-gapped parsing with Parse's Cost Effective and Agentic tiers when OCRia runs on your own GPUs. Extract and Parse's Agentic Plus tier call frontier models, and LlamaIndex managed inference needs outbound access. Reducto's deployment guide also needs more configuration detail before an offline claim can be evaluated. For offline use, confirm that models, licensing and updates work without outbound access.

## Which platforms offer single-tenant SaaS?

LlamaParse, Unstructured, Hyperscience and Tungsten document dedicated vendor-operated options. Ask which resources are dedicated: workers, storage, databases and model endpoints can have different boundaries. Reducto's dedicated hybrid workers do not establish that every component is single-tenant. Extend's dedicated BYOC environment is likewise distinct from single-tenant SaaS.

## Can I keep processing in the EU?

LlamaParse documents North American and [EU processing regions](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/regions/). Google offers [EU locations](https://cloud.google.com/document-ai/docs/regions); Azure and AWS availability depends on the service and resource. Extend, Reducto, ABBYY, Hyperscience and Tungsten describe EU options.

Check inference, backups, logs and support access alongside storage. An EU bucket alone does not establish EU processing.

## Does self-hosted parsing still call an LLM?

It can. LlamaParse separates where the platform runs from where inference runs. Depending on the configuration, you can use supported model providers with your credentials, host supported models on your own GPUs, or use LlamaIndex-managed inference. Some processing steps can still require external frontier models.

Reducto Full VPC supports its own models and external integrations. Extend BYOC uses customer-account cloud-native AI services, while its hybrid option uses vendor-side inference.

Distinguish “same cloud provider” from “same account.” Confirm the endpoint and contractual processing boundary for every model call. For offline deployments, all required inference must execute within the disconnected environment; the location of the parser's API server is insufficient.

## What should you know about each vendor?

### Azure Document Intelligence

[Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/document-intelligence/containers/disconnected) offers hosted processing and supported containers. Disconnected use requires approval and licensing. Match the required model version to its deployment support. See [LlamaParse vs Azure Document Intelligence](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-azure-document-intelligence).

### Google Document AI

[Document AI](https://cloud.google.com/document-ai/docs/security) offers regional hosted processors and service-perimeter controls. Evaluate it when vendor-operated regional processing is acceptable; verify processor availability in the chosen region. See [LlamaParse vs Document AI](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-document-ai).

### Amazon Textract

[Textract PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/vpc-interface-endpoints.html) provides private access to the hosted API. Check region and downstream processing. This is not software installed in your account. See [LlamaParse vs Amazon Textract](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-amazon-textract).

### ABBYY Vantage

[Vantage](https://www.abbyy.com/vantage/) offers ABBYY-hosted cloud on Azure in the US, the Netherlands and Australia, and [Vantage Private Cloud](https://docs.abbyy.com/vantage/documentation/tenant-admin/architecture/architecture), which runs on your own Kubernetes infrastructure. Clarify model dependencies and update paths for the proposed private-cloud setup. See [LlamaParse vs ABBYY Vantage](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-abby-vantage).

### Tungsten TotalAgility

[TotalAgility](https://www.tungstenautomation.com/products/totalagility/), from Tungsten Automation (formerly Kofax), offers cloud and on-premises workflows. Confirm dedicated hosting, network isolation and account ownership separately. See [LlamaParse vs Kofax](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-kofax).

### Hyperscience

[Hyperscience](https://www.hyperscience.ai/platform/hypercell/) offers SaaS, private tenants and customer-controlled deployments. Its SaaS is hosted mostly in the US and Frankfurt. Hyperscience [says it can run in air-gapped environments](https://www.hyperscience.ai/blog/infrastructure-enhancement-for-scalability-and-choice/); its FedRAMP High SaaS, built with Palantir, is a separate hosted offering. For offline use, confirm the support scope.

### Mathpix

[Mathpix Private Cloud OCR](https://mathpix.com/private-cloud-ocr) supports customer infrastructure and disconnected operation. Check hardware, document formats, page allowance and optional connectivity for the quoted configuration.

### Datalab

[Datalab](https://documentation.datalab.to/docs/on-prem/overview) offers an enterprise container and states offline support. Confirm models, hardware and licensing; installing Marker is a separate offering.

### Reducto

[Reducto](https://docs.reducto.ai/onprem/enterprise_deployment_options) distinguishes hybrid from Full VPC. Establish inference location, dedicated components and external integrations for the selected setup. See [LlamaParse vs Reducto](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-reducto).

### Unstructured

[Unstructured](https://docs.unstructured.io/overview-deploy-enterprise) offers shared SaaS, a dedicated instance in its own cloud, and In-VPC deployment in your AWS, Azure or GCP account. Identify where connectors, orchestration, enrichment and models run. The OSS library has a different scope. See [LlamaParse vs Unstructured](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-unstructured).

### Extend

[Extend BYOC](https://docs.extend.ai/security/deployment-options) uses customer-account cloud-native AI services. Hybrid uses vendor-side inference. Fully air-gapped operation is explicitly excluded. See [LlamaParse vs Extend](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-extend-ai).

### LlamaParse

[LlamaParse](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/) offers managed, single-tenant, BYOC and on-premises options. Enterprise self-hosting includes Parse and Extract. Inference is configured separately: use supported providers, supported local models or LlamaIndex-managed inference. Availability depends on the setup, and external model calls may still be required. Air-gapped parsing is supported for Parse's Cost Effective and Agentic tiers when OCRia runs on your own GPUs; Extract and Agentic Plus need outbound model calls.

### Docling and local OCR tools

[Docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) supports local execution with separately provisioned models. PaddleOCR and Tesseract are additional local OCR components. Your team owns operations and integration. See [LlamaParse vs Docling](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-docling).

## How should you narrow the shortlist?

| Requirement | First evaluation | Alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processing in your cloud account | LlamaParse BYOC | Reducto Full VPC; Extend BYOC |
| EU processing without operating the stack | Regional managed LlamaParse | Required-region Azure or Google processor |
| No internet access at runtime | LlamaParse Cost Effective or Agentic, with OCRia on your GPUs | Azure disconnected containers; Mathpix |
| Dedicated infrastructure operated by a vendor | LlamaParse single-tenant | Unstructured or Hyperscience private tenant |
| Lowest operating effort | Regional managed service | Dedicated SaaS if isolation is required |
| Open-source software only | Docling with suitable model licenses | Local OCR components plus your own pipeline |

These are architecture-based starting points, not a measured accuracy ranking. Verify contract scope separately: a vendor's SOC 2 report, HIPAA-related offering or GDPR commitments do not establish that every product, region and deployment is covered.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is LlamaParse hosted-only?

No. Its deployment documentation lists managed SaaS, single-tenant SaaS, BYOC and on-premises options. Self-hosting is an Enterprise offering.

### Do self-hosted deployments still call an LLM?

Some do. Platform hosting and inference are separate choices, and even local document-model configurations can use external frontier models.

### Can I use Azure OpenAI or Bedrock instead of public model APIs?

LlamaParse documents Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI integrations. Confirm that the selected models, regions and endpoint configuration meet your processing boundary.

### Does a VPC endpoint keep processing in my account?

It provides private network access to a service. It does not, by itself, deploy that service's processing software in your account.

### How does self-hosting cost compare with an API?

Compare license and support fees, compute, storage, idle capacity and operational work against your actual page volume. A page allowance divided into a contract price is not the full cost per page; hardware utilization and required model calls also matter.

Read the [LlamaParse deployment guide](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/) and [contact the team](https://www.llamaindex.ai/contact) to discuss self-hosted access.

# Best PDF Data Extraction Software in 2026: 13 Tools Compared

*Published by LlamaIndex, which develops LlamaParse Extract and the *[*ExtractBench*](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench)* benchmark. We include our own product and identify where independent comparison data is missing.*

**What's the best PDF data extraction software overall?** Our recommendation is LlamaParse Extract for production workflows spanning invoices, bank statements, financial reports, contracts and insurance records. Its combination of schema-guided JSON, repeated-record extraction, source evidence and deployment options is the basis for that recommendation. Agentic Plus scores 96.17 Value F1 on the cited standard ExtractBench snapshot; the separate Pro results below address more difficult documents. It works through a standalone API or web UI without requiring the LlamaIndex framework.

- **Best overall extraction starting point:** LlamaParse Extract
- **Invoices, bank statements and financial documents:** LlamaParse Extract with explicit line-item, transaction and reconciliation checks
- **Demanding layouts and interpretation:** Agentic Plus; use the Pro results as evidence for the difficult-document trial
- **Quality and cost optimization:** Compare LlamaParse tiers at a fixed acceptance threshold
- **Existing cloud or review-system requirements:** Compare integrations and operating needs after qualifying extraction quality

## Where does LlamaExtract lead on difficult-document extraction?

The standard ExtractBench average is only part of the choice. In the pinned ExtractBench Pro snapshot, LlamaExtract Agentic Plus scores 77.70 Value F1 and 38% perfect documents, versus 73.87 and 34% for Extend Operator, 56.35 and 3% for Reducto Deep, and 43.93 and 2% for Datalab Accurate. These results give buyers a concrete reason to evaluate LlamaExtract when unusual layouts and interpretation rules cause expensive failures. [Pinned Pro results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard-pro.csv).

Pro uses 100 synthetic long-tail documents and a 30-minute policy; perfect documents means 100% Value F1 within that test. It is not an invoice posting or straight-through-processing rate. LlamaIndex publishes the benchmark. The standard ExtractBench near-tie with Reducto Deep Extract and each product’s tested configuration should remain visible alongside this long-tail advantage.

## PDF data extraction software compared

PDF data extraction is not the same as converting a PDF into plain text. Extraction returns the specific fields and records your workflow needs, usually as structured JSON. A purchase order might require vendor name, PO number, delivery dates and every line item, including evidence of where each value was found.

The table compares what each tool is useful for, how you configure it, the evidence it returns and its pricing. Published field-extraction results are discussed below the table.

| Software | Documented scope | Setup | Citations / confidence | Cost per 1,000 pages | Deployment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**LlamaParse Extract**](https://www.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse) | Production extraction across invoices, financial reports, contracts and insurance records | JSON schema, no training | Source evidence and field-level confidence | \$10 to \$75, including parsing | Managed, single tenant, BYOC, on-prem |
| [Docsumo](https://www.docsumo.com/) | Operations with human review | No templates claimed; review workflow | Confidence; citations not established | Quote | Cloud |
| [ABBYY Vantage](https://www.abbyy.com/vantage/) | Established enterprise document workflows | Pretrained and trainable skills | Not established in public docs | Quote | Cloud; private cloud on your Kubernetes |
| [Nanonets](https://nanonets.com/) | Configurable extraction workflows | No templates claimed | Confidence; citations not established | \$0.30 per page for AI extraction, plus other blocks | Cloud, VPC, on-prem |
| [Rossum](https://rossum.ai/) | Invoice processing and review | Learns from corrections | Confidence; citations not established | From \$18,000/year | Cloud |
| [Google Document AI](https://cloud.google.com/document-ai) | Prebuilt and custom extraction on GCP | Prebuilt or Custom Extractor | Confidence and boxes | \$10 Invoice; \$30 Custom | Google Cloud |
| [Azure AI Document Intelligence](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-foundry/tools/document-intelligence) | Invoices and extraction on Azure | Prebuilt or labeled training | Confidence and boxes | See regional pricing | Azure, some containers |
| [Amazon Textract](https://aws.amazon.com/textract/) | Forms and expenses on AWS | Prebuilt Expense, Queries | Confidence and boxes | \$10 Expense; \$50 Forms | AWS |
| [Adobe PDF Extract API](https://developer.adobe.com/document-services/apis/pdf-extract/) | PDF elements for downstream processing | Developer code | No field-level citations/confidence | Quote; free transactions | Adobe cloud |
| [PyMuPDF](https://pymupdf.readthedocs.io/) | Code-based extraction from consistent PDFs | Developer code | Developer-built | Free/open or commercial license | Local |
| [pdfplumber](https://github.com/jsvine/pdfplumber) | Inspecting and extracting text-based PDFs | Developer code | Developer-built | Free software | Local |
| [Camelot and Tabula](https://camelot-py.readthedocs.io/) | Tables in consistently formatted PDFs | Developer code | Developer-built | Free software | Local |
| [Docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) | Local conversion before field extraction | Developer code | Developer-built | Free software | Local |

**Price notes:** These are different product tiers and billing units, not a normalized price-performance ranking. LlamaParse includes the parsing-plus-extraction credits. Nanonets charges per block run; its AI extraction block runs once per page. Docsumo, ABBYY and Adobe require quotes. The open-source options have engineering and compute costs even without a license or API fee.

## How were these tools evaluated?

[ExtractBench](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench) evaluates schema-guided extraction on **370 documents and 4,869 pages** across 67 document types and eight domains. It scores the correctness and completeness of values, repeated records, nulls and source grounding using **Value F1** and grounding metrics. We use the public leaderboard snapshot from **October 30, 2026**. Its documents include SEC filings, tax forms, procurement and customs paperwork, healthcare remittances, energy filings and other complex records. It is **not** a uniform 13-product test on invoices, bank statements and contracts.

For tables, we cite [ParseBench](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench) at leaderboard commit [0ccc167](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/commit/0ccc16783612a8ff37e77139f5e799510cde47b6) (November 2, 2026), which tests how well parsers preserve table structure. That number should not be read as the extraction system's field accuracy.

Among the vendors with public ExtractBench runs, LlamaParse Extract Agentic Plus scores **96.17** and Reducto Deep Extract scores **96.08**, only **0.09 points apart**. LlamaParse Extract records **83.25 word-level grounding F1**, versus **50.76 for Reducto Deep Extract** in that snapshot. See [LlamaParse vs Reducto](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-reducto). These figures describe the benchmarked configurations; the other products are compared by their documented capabilities.

## Which AI extraction platforms are best for structured fields?

### 1. LlamaParse Extract: best overall for production document extraction

[LlamaParse Extract](https://www.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse) accepts a JSON schema or Pydantic model and returns structured JSON, including repeated records. It does not require training a separate model for each document layout. Optional source citations identify page, text and bounding-box evidence for fields, and grounded confidence returns a 0–1 score for individual values.

Its **Agentic Plus tier scores 96.17 Value F1**, **Agentic scores 95.65** and **Cost Effective scores 94.21** on the October ExtractBench snapshot. Including parsing, the tiers cost **\$75, \$31.25 and \$10 per 1,000 pages**, respectively. It supports managed cloud, single-tenant and private deployment options, including BYOC and on-premises. It is especially useful when document formats vary but the required JSON schema is stable.

### 2. Docsumo: extraction and review-workflow features

[Docsumo](https://www.docsumo.com/) is an intelligent document processing platform with extraction, per-field confidence and review workflows. It targets operational documents such as invoices and statements and markets template-free processing.

Docsumo advertises high field accuracy and straight-through processing, but those figures are vendor claims, not directly comparable ExtractBench results. Its review workflow is a feature to evaluate against the buyer’s operating requirements. Compare LlamaParse’s extraction quality and the selected review integration rather than assuming that a packaged queue establishes a better overall solution.

### 3. ABBYY Vantage: trained document skills and workflow configuration

[ABBYY Vantage](https://www.abbyy.com/vantage/) provides pre-trained document skills, a low-code design environment and options for training new skills. Its catalog covers familiar business documents, including invoices.

The advantage is its operational tooling and deployment flexibility: ABBYY-hosted cloud in the US, EU and Australia, or Vantage Private Cloud on your own Kubernetes infrastructure. The tradeoffs are implementation complexity, custom training for some document types and quote-based pricing. ABBYY Vantage does not have a public ExtractBench score in the available comparison, and its public documentation does not establish field-level citation behavior. See [LlamaParse vs ABBYY Vantage](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-abby-vantage).

### 4. Nanonets: for configurable AI extraction workflows

[Nanonets](https://nanonets.com/) offers an extraction platform and API with JSON output and confidence information. Its current positioning emphasizes processing different layouts without per-format templates or prompt engineering, with cloud, VPC and on-premises options.

Pricing is per block run rather than a single per-page fee. The AI data extraction block costs **\$0.30 per run** and runs once per page, about **\$300 per 1,000 pages** at list price before import, export and other blocks. Volume plans are discounted. Vendor accuracy claims are not independent ExtractBench scores. Nanonets is worth evaluating when workflow configuration and private deployment matter.

### 5. Rossum: transactional-document extraction and review

[Rossum](https://rossum.ai/) is oriented toward transactional documents, especially invoices. It combines extraction, exception handling and a review workflow, and learns from user corrections instead of requiring a fixed template for every supplier.

Rossum documents per-field confidence thresholds and a 14-day trial. Its entry pricing starts at **\$18,000 per year** with a one-year minimum contract, making it more relevant to teams with ongoing invoice volume than occasional API users. Rossum has no public ExtractBench score for a direct accuracy comparison.

## Which cloud document AI tools are best?

### 6. Google Document AI: prebuilt and custom processors

[Google Document AI](https://cloud.google.com/document-ai) offers prebuilt document processors and a Custom Extractor that can work with few or no examples in some modes. It returns extracted entities with confidence scores and page evidence.

The **Invoice Parser costs \$10 per 1,000 pages**, and the **Custom Extractor \$30 per 1,000 pages** (\$20 above 1 million pages a month). Google's Layout Parser scores **54.95 on ParseBench tables**, but that is not a field-extraction accuracy score for the Custom Extractor. Treat the existing cloud environment as an integration requirement; compare LlamaParse’s extraction quality and total operating fit before choosing a processor. See [LlamaParse vs Document AI](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-document-ai).

### 7. Azure AI Document Intelligence: prebuilt and custom models

[Azure AI Document Intelligence](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-foundry/tools/document-intelligence) offers Read, Layout, prebuilt invoice and other document models, plus custom models that can be trained on labeled examples.

Azure Layout scores **85.97 on ParseBench tables**, the strongest of the three hyperscaler parsers in this comparison. Prebuilt and custom extraction have different rates; see [Azure's regional pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/ai-document-intelligence/). An existing Microsoft deployment does not establish extraction superiority; qualify the Azure and LlamaParse configurations on the same required records. See [LlamaParse vs Azure Document Intelligence](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-azure-document-intelligence).

### 8. Amazon Textract: forms, queries and expense APIs

[Amazon Textract](https://aws.amazon.com/textract/) provides text recognition, forms, tables, Queries and Analyze Expense. Expense processing returns fields and line items for invoices and receipts, with confidence values and bounding boxes.

Analyze Expense is **\$10 per 1,000 pages** at the listed tier, while Forms processing can cost **\$50 per 1,000 pages**. Textract's parser scores **84.46 on ParseBench tables**. Its AWS integration is documented, but this comparison has no matched ExtractBench field-accuracy result for Analyze Expense. Invoice buyers should evaluate LlamaParse Extract directly rather than selecting on the cloud provider alone. See [LlamaParse vs Amazon Textract](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-amazon-textract).

### 9. Adobe PDF Extract API: for turning PDFs into elements developers can process

[Adobe PDF Extract API](https://developer.adobe.com/document-services/apis/pdf-extract/) converts native and scanned PDFs into structured document content, including tables and figures. It can deliver tables as CSV or XLSX and integrate through developer SDKs.

It is a **parsing API, not a schema-based field extractor**. To obtain a JSON object of specific invoice or contract fields, developers need additional logic or a model. Adobe offers a free tier of 500 document transactions, while paid pricing is by quote. It is useful when developers primarily need reliable PDF components to feed another system.

## Which open-source libraries are best for extracting data from PDFs?

These libraries are useful for programmatic extraction from born-digital PDFs. Unlike schema-guided AI extraction services, they usually require code to identify which values belong to which fields.

### 10. PyMuPDF: for fast PDF text and layout processing

[PyMuPDF](https://pymupdf.readthedocs.io/) provides text, geometry and table extraction from PDFs. PyMuPDF4LLM adds Markdown conversion; OCR can be integrated when needed.

PyMuPDF4LLM scores **56.93 on ParseBench's table dimension**, while a plain text-extraction configuration scores zero on that dimension. That distinction matters: simply retrieving a PDF's text layer does not reconstruct its tables. PyMuPDF is useful when developers control the input format and can write their own extraction rules. Review its AGPL/commercial licensing before deployment.

### 11. pdfplumber: for inspecting text-based PDFs

[pdfplumber](https://github.com/jsvine/pdfplumber) exposes PDF characters, coordinates, lines and table-like structures through a Python interface. It is useful for extracting data from consistent, machine-generated PDFs and debugging page layouts.

It does not perform OCR itself, and it is not a schema-driven field extraction service. Developers need to write logic for field recognition and error handling. There is no public ExtractBench or ParseBench result for it in the cited snapshot.

### 12. Camelot and Tabula: for extracting tables from consistent PDFs

[Camelot](https://camelot-py.readthedocs.io/) and [Tabula](https://tabula.technology/) focus on turning tables in PDFs into machine-readable data. They are popular for reports and regularly formatted statements, particularly when the PDF contains selectable text.

They do not solve general document understanding or schema extraction. Tabula is text-PDF-oriented, while Camelot has additional processing options. Neither has a directly comparable field-extraction benchmark score in the current research.

### 13. Docling: for local document conversion

[Docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) is an MIT-licensed document conversion toolkit with support for Markdown, HTML and structured JSON representations, including table processing and OCR integrations.

The public ParseBench Docling-models configuration scores **66.41 on tables**; the leaderboard marks it unverified because its published outputs are incomplete. It does not provide a general-purpose schema-to-fields extraction capability out of the box. It is a strong option when the goal is to build an internal document pipeline and developers can add their own extraction layer. See [LlamaParse vs Docling](https://www.llamaindex.ai/compare/llamaparse-vs-docling).

## Which PDF data extraction tool should you choose?

| Your requirement | First option to evaluate | Selection test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best overall schema-guided extraction | LlamaParse Extract | Value accuracy, complete records, grounding and operating fit |
| Invoices and receipts | LlamaParse Extract | Supplier, currency, totals, every line item and source evidence |
| Bank statements and financial reports | LlamaParse Extract | All transactions, entity and period labels, units and reconciliation |
| Long contracts and difficult documents | LlamaParse Extract Agentic Plus | Cross-page meaning, obligations, exceptions and supporting evidence |
| Insurance claims and underwriting records | LlamaParse with Classify, Split and Extract as needed | Packet identity, required fields, exceptions and review policy |
| Scanned forms and changing layouts | LlamaParse Extract | Readability, null handling and schema accuracy |
| High-volume extraction with human review | LlamaParse Extract plus the chosen review workflow | Errors accepted, exceptions reviewed and reviewer effort |
| Lower processing cost | Compare LlamaParse tiers first | Cost per usable record at the same quality requirement |
| Open-source software or fixed-template text extraction required | Evaluate a local library separately | Full implementation scope and maintenance cost |

LlamaParse is our overall recommendation across these business workflows. The recommendation combines published extraction evidence with documented capabilities; it is not a claim that all 13 products were tested on every invoice, insurance or banking task. Qualify the implementation using the same ground truth, schema and acceptance rules for every candidate.

## Frequently asked questions

### What's the difference between PDF parsing and PDF data extraction?

Parsing turns a PDF into text, Markdown or layout-aware document elements. Data extraction returns named fields in a target schema, such as invoice number, total and line items, often with page-level evidence. [ParseBench](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench) measures parsing; [ExtractBench](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench) measures schema-guided extraction.

### Do I need a template for each PDF layout?

Not always. Schema-driven systems such as LlamaParse Extract take a target schema rather than a fixed template. Google Custom Extractor also supports foundation-model modes with few or no samples, while other custom workflows may require labeled examples or training.

### Can PDF data extraction software handle scanned documents?

Many AI and cloud tools include OCR and can process scans. Python utilities such as pdfplumber and Tabula assume selectable text, while PyMuPDF needs an OCR integration for scanned pages. Test low-resolution scans, handwriting and rotated pages rather than relying on a vendor-wide yes/no claim.

### How do I measure extraction accuracy before buying?

Create a representative test set, define the same JSON schema for every tool and score correct values, missing fields, repeated records and source grounding. You can use the public [ExtractBench harness](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench) or run a smaller internal evaluation on real documents, including hard exceptions.

### Is PDF data extraction the same as web scraping?

No. PDF extraction reads files and produces structured information from their contents. Web scraping collects information from websites. Broad software categories sometimes mix the two, so make sure you evaluate tools meant for document processing.

## Try LlamaParse Extract on your documents

[LlamaParse Extract](https://www.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse) accepts a schema and returns structured JSON with optional source citations and field confidence. The free plan includes **10,000 credits per month**, enough to test extraction on representative documents before choosing a tier.

You can also inspect the [ExtractBench evaluation code](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench) and [ParseBench table results](https://www.parsebench.ai/) to see what the public measurements cover.

# Reducto vs LlamaParse and LlamaExtract Pricing: Quality per Accepted Document

LlamaExtract’s published results give buyers specific accuracy and grounding advantages to weigh against Reducto’s processing costs. Standard ExtractBench has nearly tied overall value scores for Agentic Plus and Deep Extract, while the Pro snapshot shows a larger gap on difficult documents. Price the configuration that meets your acceptance rule, including review, rather than comparing unrelated Parse and Extract rates.

## Where LlamaExtract performs better on ExtractBench

| Configuration | Value F1 | Word grounding | Recorded cost per 1,000 pages (\$) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaExtract Agentic Plus | 96.17 | 83.25 | 75.00 |
| LlamaExtract Agentic | 95.65 | 82.33 | 31.20 |
| Reducto Deep Extract | 96.08 | 50.76 | 63.50 |

The standard suite records Agentic at \$31.20 per 1,000 pages and 95.65 Value F1, while Agentic Plus and Reducto Deep Extract score 96.17 and 96.08 at \$75.00 and \$63.50. Plus is more expensive here; its case depends on the grounding and long-tail results rather than the lowest page price. On Pro, Plus reaches 77.70 Value F1 and 38% perfect documents versus 56.35 and 3% for Reducto Deep. [Pro results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard-pro.csv).

These are published results from the pinned ExtractBench snapshot at commit 7004e29, checked on November 4, 2026. The suite covers 370 documents and 4,869 pages. Value F1 measures extracted values; it is not a straight-through-processing rate. LlamaIndex publishes the benchmark and develops LlamaExtract, now documented within LlamaParse Extract. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv), [methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/docs/extractbench.md).

## Start with the right product rate

The reviewed rate card, effective September 1, lists \$10 per 1,000 pages for r-1 Parse, \$20 for Extract and \$40 for Deep Extract. Extraction pricing includes parsing rather than automatically requiring an additional Parse charge. Contracts and optional features can change the applicable total. These figures are a dated list-price reference, not an account-specific quote. [Reducto usage and pricing](https://docs.reducto.ai/reference/credit-usage)

The product distinction matters immediately. A one-cent parsing result should not be compared with another vendor's fully configured extraction result as if both purchased the same output. First decide whether the application needs document content, schema-defined fields or a more involved extraction workflow.

Only then should the team compare the rates for configurations that meet that requirement.

## Build a workflow bill of materials

Use a bill of materials for the workflow. Include the API operations needed to produce the output, any optional processing, application infrastructure and the work required when automation does not finish the job.

| Cost category | Input to collect |
| --- | --- |
| Processing | Applicable product rate and billable volume |
| Features | Required citations, charts or other options |
| Exceptions | Frequency and handling cost of incomplete outputs |
| Review | Minutes spent verifying or correcting results |
| Integration | Ongoing engineering and operational effort |
| Delay | Business consequence of waiting for usable output |

Keep one-time implementation cost separate from recurring operating cost. A small pilot may be dominated by integration effort, while a high-volume deployment may be dominated by processing and review.

Also distinguish documents from pages. Two workloads with the same page count can require different numbers of review decisions and different downstream actions.

## One minute versus three minutes of review

Consider an illustrative workload of 10,000 one-page documents. Suppose configuration A costs \$0.02 per document and sends 5% of documents to review. Configuration B costs \$0.04 and sends 2% to review. Assume each reviewed document takes one minute and reviewer time costs \$30 per hour.

These are invented scenario inputs, not measured Reducto or LlamaIndex results. Configuration A would have \$200 in processing charges and \$250 in review time, for \$450 before other costs. Configuration B would have \$400 in processing charges and \$100 in review time, for \$500.

Under those assumptions, the lower processing rate remains cheaper. If review takes three minutes instead, the totals become \$950 and \$700. The conclusion changes because review effort changes, not because one vendor was assigned an automatic accuracy advantage.

Replace the scenario inputs with applicable pricing and measured review effort before using the result in a purchasing decision.

## Define “accepted” before dividing by it

Define an accepted document before estimating cost per accepted document. A result may require correct fields, complete records, sufficient evidence and successful downstream validation. Merely returning an API response does not necessarily satisfy that contract.

Track false acceptance separately from review. A workflow that quietly accepts incorrect outputs can appear inexpensive because it avoids review, while creating costs elsewhere. Do not reward that behavior in the calculator.

Report the numerator and denominator explicitly. Total operating cost divided by accepted documents is useful only when the acceptance standard is consistent across configurations. If one workflow includes manual correction, count that work and state that the final result is assisted rather than fully automated.

## Measure when the application can use the result

Use the application's time to a usable result. Reducto documents concurrency behavior in which work can queue, so service processing duration alone may differ from what the caller experiences. [Reducto concurrency throttling](https://docs.reducto.ai/reference/throttling)

The Python SDK also documents automatic retries for selected failures. Retry behavior affects elapsed time and should be recorded, but the reviewed SDK behavior does not establish that every retry produces an additional billable charge. Do not invent a double-billing assumption. [Reducto Python SDK](https://github.com/reductoai/reducto-python-sdk)

For an overnight batch, a longer turnaround may be acceptable. For an interactive workflow, a similar delay may create abandonment or require a different user experience. Evaluate latency against the business process rather than a universal preference for the smallest number.

## Confirm the quote before publishing the comparison

Check the account rate card, billing units and enabled features. The reviewed Reducto chart documentation and pricing page contain inconsistent language about advanced-chart charges, so chart-heavy totals need confirmation. [Chart extraction documentation](https://docs.reducto.ai/configs/parse/chart-extraction)

The published LlamaExtract quality and grounding results supply concrete reasons to include it in the cost trial. Keep the calculator’s assumptions visible so the actual quote, review work and accepted outputs determine the economical choice.

### Can a benchmark score stand in for a review rate?

No. Review depends on the workload and the acceptance policy. Measure how often people intervene and how long the intervention takes. A benchmark percentage does not supply those inputs.

### Should Parse be added to every Extract charge?

The reviewed Reducto rate card includes parsing in extraction pricing. Adding both automatically would overstate that workflow’s listed cost; check the applicable configuration and contract.

Use the published results to choose the LlamaExtract tier worth pricing, with grounding and long-tail requirements explicit. Compare the actual Reducto alternative, then replace benchmark page costs with current quotes and measured acceptance rates. Select the complete workflow on accepted-document cost rather than claiming that Plus is always the cheapest page.

# Extend vs LlamaParse: BYOC, Hybrid and Data Retention

LlamaParse and Extend should be compared using the infrastructure and retention arrangement you would actually buy. Put the proposed LlamaParse deployment beside Extend BYOC or Hybrid, then trace document content through storage, inference, evaluation data and support access. Zero-data-retention terminology does not replace that configuration-specific map.

*Published by LlamaIndex. This is technical procurement guidance, not a legal opinion or a determination that a particular deployment meets a customer's obligations.*

## Put the LlamaParse deployment in the comparison

LlamaParse documents managed, single-tenant and customer-controlled deployment options. Use that as a concrete starting point for a private-processing proposal, then name the tier, model dependencies and any external calls in the configuration being evaluated. [LlamaParse deployment documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/).

Compare storage, inference, telemetry, support access and update delivery as separate rows. For an offline requirement, confirm which tiers and models can run without external services; do not extend that property to every configuration. [Can LlamaParse run on-premises?](/agents/llamaparse-on-premises) covers the LlamaIndex side of that review.

Benchmark quality is a reason to shortlist a parser. It does not prove private-deployment accuracy, air-gap compliance or an identical result across hosted and self-hosted configurations.

## How do the deployment options differ?

Extend documents managed US/EU hosting, BYOC in the customer's cloud account and Hybrid with customer-side storage but inference in Extend's cloud. It states that fully air-gapped deployment is not currently offered. [Deployment documentation](https://docs.extend.ai/security/deployment-options).

| Option | Key boundary to investigate |
| --- | --- |
| Managed cloud | Vendor-managed storage, processing and regional arrangements |
| BYOC | Customer-cloud resources, AI services and operational responsibilities |
| Hybrid | Customer-side storage combined with external inference processing |
| Air-gapped requirement | Whether the required isolation is actually supported |

Choose against the organization's permitted processing locations and operating capacity. BYOC adds a deployment option, but its presence alone does not establish that an isolation requirement is met.

## Why is storage residency insufficient as a single requirement?

A document can be stored in one environment and processed in another. It can also generate derived content: extracted text, thumbnails, model inputs, logs, evaluation labels and final results.

A useful data-flow map follows each artifact through collection, processing, retention and deletion. Ask which system receives the original file, which receives derived text and which stores the output. Then identify the operator and contractual boundary for each stage.

For Hybrid specifically, Extend states that documents are sent to its cloud for inference even though documents and application data reside on the customer side. [Hybrid processing description](https://docs.extend.ai/security/deployment-options).

## Two policies, two different deployment decisions

Imagine a hypothetical company whose policy allows sensitive files to be stored only in its own cloud account but permits processing by approved external services. Hybrid might be a candidate, subject to the approved providers and contractual terms.

Now change the policy: no document content may leave a specified isolated environment for processing. The same deployment label no longer answers the requirement. The team must establish the actual inference path and whether the required isolation is supported.

In these hypothetical policies, the decisive difference is permission to process content externally. Write that requirement explicitly. “Must be on-prem” leaves too much room for stakeholders to mean different things.

## What does ZDR mean for evaluation data?

Extend documents a retention exception for evaluation sets: their files and expected outputs remain protected from ordinary workspace retention, including ZDR, while evaluation-run outputs follow the retention schedule. Removing a file from all evaluation sets changes that protection. [Evaluation retention rules](https://docs.extend.ai/evaluation/overview).

This distinction has a practical purpose: stable evaluation data supports repeated comparisons. It also means an organization must deliberately manage which sensitive files become long-lived test assets.

Create an evaluation-data owner and a deletion process. Record why each set exists, what information it contains and when it should be reviewed. Do not assume an operational deletion policy automatically covers every development or testing artifact.

When possible, use appropriately sanitized or synthetic test cases for examples that do not require real sensitive content. Have the responsible reviewer confirm whether that treatment is sufficient for the applicable obligation.

## Which provider and model questions should be asked?

Ask for the relevant inference providers, contractual no-training terms, retention arrangements and available provider restrictions. Extend documents model/provider controls and subprocessors' data-handling commitments; the precise agreement should be verified for the intended deployment. [Data handling](https://docs.extend.ai/security/data-handling).

Do not infer a universal backend from one infrastructure example. Extend's BYOC documentation mentions cloud-native AI services such as Vertex AI, but that does not establish the model or OCR supplier for every service configuration. [BYOC requirements](https://docs.extend.ai/security/deployment-options).

If independent operation is required, ask specifically about model weights and external service dependencies. A public SDK establishes access to the client code; it does not answer either question.

## How should operational responsibility be compared?

For each option, assign responsibility for provisioning, updates, incident response, monitoring, backup and deletion. A more customer-controlled deployment can bring additional operating work. A managed deployment can reduce that work while introducing different vendor dependencies.

Ask how updates are approved and how a previous configuration is restored. Determine who can access document content during support and what evidence of deletion or access is available.

These questions should be answered with deployment-specific documentation and contracts. A generic security badge or architecture diagram is useful context but not a substitute for the required operating commitments.

## Use the same data-flow map for LlamaIndex

Ask LlamaIndex to document the same storage, inference, retention and support-access paths for the proposed deployment. Compare each path with the written policy. Extend's multiple deployment patterns give buyers options, but the choice still depends on the processing arrangement and the retained artifacts the organization can approve.

## Get agreement on one data-flow map

Request a LlamaParse private-deployment proposal alongside the competitor’s proposal and compare the complete data flows. Confirm offline model availability, operational dependencies and update delivery in the exact configuration. Use the architecture review to qualify the deployment and a representative document trial to qualify its output.
