title: "ParseArena and PAIR vs ParseBench-2: How to Evaluate Document Parsers"
description: "Compare LLM-as-a-judge and severity-tuned deterministic evaluation for document parsing. Use both to create a repeatable, task-aware acceptance test."
published: "2026-11-16"
updated: "2026-11-16"
source: "https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-parsebench-v2"
---

# ParseArena and PAIR vs ParseBench-2: How to Evaluate Document Parsers

## Short answer

ParseArena and PAIR are useful for a real problem: document parses can preserve the same information in different valid representations, and a fixed string or markup rule can punish the wrong thing. ParseBench-2 and Metric Lab address a different problem: a single LLM-as-a-judge prompt is not, on its own, a sufficiently repeatable or granular production evaluation.

The strongest approach combines both ideas. Start from human preferences about which failures matter, build deterministic tests around those preferences, validate that scoring against human review and a judge where it is helpful, then run the resulting framework repeatedly as models, prompts and documents change.

## What ParseArena and PAIR measure

Reducto’s ParseArena evaluates parser output on a public enterprise-document set. Its PAIR methodology presents an original page and two blinded parser outputs to an LLM judge, repeats each comparison three times, and reports a win rate against a shared baseline. Ties count as half a win. [Reducto’s PAIR methodology](https://reducto.ai/blog/pairwise-ai-ranking-parse-evaluation) and [r-1 mini announcement](https://reducto.ai/blog/reducto-r-1-mini-parse-model) describe the approach and the vendor’s reported results.

This format can recognize semantic equivalence that a simplistic deterministic rule misses. For example, two tables expressed in different supported formats may retain the same cell relationships, and a judge can assess the page alongside both outputs rather than requiring one exact serialization.

PAIR’s public description also documents its limits: the score is pairwise, relative to a selected baseline, dependent on the judge model and prompt, and expressed as wins, ties and losses. It should be read as evidence for a particular evaluation setup, not as a universal measure of every document workflow.

## What ParseBench-2 and Metric Lab measure

ParseBench-2 is an open benchmark and metric-design framework for document parsing. It evaluates text, formatting, tables, charts, visual grounding and forms using a catalog of more than 330 controlled error scenarios. Each scenario has a human-defined severity policy based on the downstream consequence of the error. Equivalent Markdown and HTML representations can be treated as harmless, while a value placed under the wrong header can receive a large penalty. [The ParseBench-2 technical report](https://www.llamaindex.ai/files/parsebench-v2-severity-aware-evaluation-of-document-parsing.pdf), [open-source repository](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench), and [launch article](https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-parsebench-v2) document the data, code and policy.

### A dataset built for production failure modes

ParseBench-2 contains 4,317 page-level test cases from 2,645 documents. It expands the revised original corpus with targeted hard cases rather than relying on one document style: complex table headers, financial and insurance tables, dense tables, headings, strikeout, underline and government forms. The six dimensions are deliberately broad:

| Dimension | What a parser must preserve | Coverage in ParseBench-2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | Transcription and reading order | 508 text cases |
| Formatting | Meaningful structure, including headings and strikeout | Text plus 353 targeted formatting cases |
| Tables | Values in the right row and header relationships | 1,753 table cases across five table datasets |
| Charts | Complete data series, not a few spot-checked values | 568 chart cases and 36,958 chart values across 1,025 charts |
| Visual grounding | Source locations that point to the right text | 535 layout cases |
| Forms | Field-value pairing, checkbox state, signatures and blanks | 600 form cases, including fillable and mostly blank forms |

The corpus is not just larger. ParseBench-2 corrected and clarified ambiguous annotations in the earlier dimensions, adds more complete references, and treats blank fields and formatting state as information when they affect an agent’s decision. A parser that returns the right words in the wrong column, invents a checkbox state, drops a strikeout or assigns a value to the wrong table header has not preserved the same document.

### How ParseBench-2 turns preferences into repeatable rules

The design starts with a human judgment: how bad is this error for a downstream task? ParseBench-2 classifies controlled output perturbations as critical, major, minor or harmless, then calibrates candidate metrics against the target score change. The repository describes six severity test suites and more than 140 implemented error checks; the broader methodology uses more than 330 error scenarios across the six dimensions.

The scoring rule is designed to prevent a high average recovery rate from hiding a critical failure. A page score is the lower of its content-recovery score and a severity cap. That means an invented value, flipped negation, swapped table header or misread form value can impose a meaningful penalty even when the rest of the page is correct. Conversely, a supported Markdown-versus-HTML representation change receives no penalty when the same information and relationships survive.

This is the important robustness point: ParseBench-2 does not assume deterministic means naive string matching. It tests deterministic metrics against controlled, human-prioritized failure cases and selects the metrics that best fit the stated policy. The policy, test cases, outputs and code are open to inspect, reproduce and challenge.

### Human alignment is part of the method, not a post-hoc claim

ParseBench-2 uses expert judgments about production consequences to define its severity policy. The metrics are then hill-climbed against those labeled perturbation tests. A concrete example in the published methodology compares a 459-cell table: under the original scoring, changing a number from one value to another cost 0.13 points while rendering the correct table in Markdown instead of HTML could reduce the score to zero. Under ParseBench-2, the wrong number costs 10 points and the equivalent Markdown output costs zero.

That example does not eliminate the need for customer-specific testing. It demonstrates the property a production metric needs: it must distinguish harmful semantic errors from harmless surface variation, and it must do so consistently enough to be rerun as a parser or model changes.

Metric Lab makes the policy inspectable and editable. A team can change dimension weights or severity assignments and recompute scores from saved page results in the browser. It includes a reproduction check against the paper policy, exposes the severity cap behavior, and lets teams see how a changed policy affects individual systems and ranks. [ParseBench-2 Metric Lab](https://www.parsebench.ai/lab/index.html) is not a claim that a default score fits every workload; it is a way to see and customize the tradeoffs behind one.

## The important difference: a preference that can be tested repeatedly

An LLM judge is a reasonable starting point for articulating a preference, especially where multiple representations may be valid. But a base prompt alone cannot reliably serve as the whole measurement system.

| Evaluation question | Pairwise LLM judge | ParseBench-2 severity-tuned framework |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Can it recognize equivalent representations? | Often yes, if the prompt and model handle the case well | Yes, when equivalence is deliberately encoded and tested |
| Can it name the failure type? | Usually only at the level requested by the prompt | Yes, across explicit dimensions and error types |
| Is it repeatable across model or prompt changes? | Requires variance testing and version controls | Recomputable from the same inputs and policy |
| Can a team change what matters? | By changing the prompt or judging rubric | By editing the documented severity policy and weights |
| Can it support regression testing at scale? | Possible, but costs and stochasticity need management | Designed for deterministic, large-scale re-runs |

Neither column is sufficient by itself. A rigid metric that does not model semantic equivalence can reward the wrong output. A judge prompt that has not been challenged with controlled errors, repeated runs and human review can turn the behavior of one model and one prompt into an opaque score.

## Build the evaluation from unit tests, not a leaderboard

Start with the downstream decision. For every document class, write examples of what the parser must preserve: a number, table-header relationship, checkbox state, reading order, redaction, chart series or source location. Then create controlled changes that test each requirement. ParseBench-2 provides a concrete model for this work: choose the dimensions that matter, identify the failure types, assign a severity policy, and calibrate the score against that policy.

For each test, state the expected severity:

1. **Harmless:** a format change that preserves meaning.
2. **Minor:** an error that is visible but recoverable without affecting a decision.
3. **Major:** an error that creates meaningful manual work or a wrong intermediate record.
4. **Critical:** an error that changes a business decision, drops a required record or invents a fact.

Run deterministic metrics against these cases and measure whether their penalties fit the policy. Use an LLM judge and expert reviewers as calibration signals: do they agree that a swapped cell is worse than a harmless table-format change? Where they disagree, inspect the underlying example rather than optimizing toward an unexplained aggregate.

## Add judge evaluation with controls

LLM-as-a-judge can add value when a deterministic signal is incomplete. Use it as a controlled component:

- Blind output identities and shuffle ordering.
- Pin the judge model, prompt and inference settings.
- Run multiple trials and report disagreement or confidence intervals, not just a single winner.
- Include ties in agreement analysis rather than dropping ambiguous cases without explanation.
- Validate against adjudicated human examples across document types and failure severities.
- Keep the page, candidate outputs, prompt, judge responses and final decision for audit.

These controls make a judge informative without asking it to be the only source of truth.

## A practical acceptance-test stack

Use public benchmarks to shortlist configurations. Then evaluate each one against a private, versioned acceptance set that includes ordinary documents and the cases that create real operational cost. Score deterministic requirements, add calibrated judge review for cases where presentation equivalence matters, and inspect critical failures manually.

Track accepted-document rate, missing and extra records, evidence quality, review rate, latency and cost per accepted document. Rerun the suite after a parser, model, prompt, schema or scoring-policy change.

The goal is not to crown a permanent winner. It is to build an evaluation system that can explain what changed, why it matters and whether the latest configuration still meets the requirements of your documents.

# LiteParse vs Chandra, Marker and Surya: Local Parsing and Commercial Use

## Short answer

LiteParse is an Apache-2.0-licensed local parser for teams that need a permissive, local-first starting point. Chandra, Marker and Surya can also be evaluated locally, but code, model weights, hosted services and commercial deployment rights are separate questions. Choose the system that your organization may use under its current terms and that produces the information your application actually needs.

This article is technical guidance, not legal advice. License terms and model versions change; have the applicable agreements and source licenses reviewed for your intended use.

## Recent Datalab releases to account for

Datalab’s recent releases include Chandra 2.7 in balanced and accurate API modes, Marker 2.2.0, and Surya 0.24.0. Each release should be treated as a new configuration in an evaluation—not as proof that an older benchmark or license review applies unchanged. Check the current [Chandra repository](https://github.com/datalab-to/chandra), [Marker releases](https://github.com/datalab-to/marker/releases), and [Surya releases](https://github.com/datalab-to/surya/releases) before making a deployment decision.

## Separate the components

| Component | Question to answer |
| --- | --- |
| Application code | What license applies to the parser implementation? |
| Model weights | What terms apply to running, modifying or redistributing the weights? |
| Evaluation data | Can the documents and annotations be used as intended? |
| Dependencies | Do their licenses add obligations? |
| Hosted or on-prem service | What contract, support and data terms apply? |

LiteParse’s Apache-2.0 license covers LiteParse itself. It does not grant rights to third-party models or commercial services selected around it. [LiteParse’s repository](https://github.com/run-llama/liteparse) is the controlling public source for its code license.

## Why open weights are not a deployment decision

Public availability can make a model inspectable and easy to test. It does not necessarily mean unrestricted commercial use. Datalab’s public projects distinguish code licenses from model terms; threshold and competitive-use provisions should be read in the current source text, rather than inferred from a blog post or an earlier release.

For a local proof of concept, record the commit, model version, hardware, OCR configuration, input types and output format. For a customer-facing service, add the intended use, entity details, redistribution plan, data controls and support expectations to the review.

## Compare usable output, not just local execution

Run a representative set through LiteParse and the alternatives. Include ordinary PDFs as well as scanned forms, complex tables, charts, Office files and documents with poor image quality. Evaluate layout preservation, source locations, Markdown or structured output, latency, memory use and the manual work needed after parsing.

If a purely local workflow misses required information, evaluate a managed service separately. LlamaParse can provide a hosted or private deployment path for workflows where managed accuracy, extraction and operational support are appropriate. The relevant comparison is the complete cost and reliability of an accepted document, not whether a tool can be installed locally.

# Invoice and Financial Document Extraction with LlamaParse: From Line Items to Verified JSON

**For teams choosing an extraction platform for invoices and financial documents, our overall recommendation is LlamaParse Extract.** It accepts the schema the application needs and returns structured records, with source-evidence options for checking the extracted information. Evaluate it directly for accounts-payable inputs, statements, financial reports and supporting contracts.

Choose on usable records and evidence. The fact that a cloud provider offers a prebuilt invoice or expense endpoint does not establish that it is the better overall extraction choice.

## What should the output contain?

An invoice header alone rarely completes the job. The application may need every line item, supplier identity, currency, adjustments and tax treatment, with enough source context to explain each field.

A bank-statement workflow has a different contract: all transactions, correct signs, account ownership and period boundaries. A financial report may require units, entity names and footnotes spanning several pages.

Extract lets the application define its target schema. The documentation describes a web UI, SDKs and REST API, so evaluation is not limited to an engineering-only integration. [Extract overview](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/).

## How would an invoice become an accepted record?

Consider a hypothetical invoice with a repeated header on page two, a discount below the line-item table and a total in a different visual region.

A proposed workflow can parse the source, extract the complete line-item array and header fields, then apply the accounting application’s validation rules. Those rules should distinguish a repeated page header from another record, retain the discount and verify that the relevant totals agree under the specified rounding policy.

| Check | What the application should establish |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Supplier, invoice number and document revision are attached to the correct record |
| Completeness | Every required line item and adjustment is represented |
| Value accuracy | Amounts, quantities, dates and currency match the source |
| Evidence | A reviewer can locate the source supporting a field |
| Business acceptance | Required external checks and approvals have passed |

Source evidence helps investigation. It does not replace the application’s payment authorization or supplier-verification policy. LlamaIndex describes invoice-processing workflows that combine parsing, extraction, validation and routing; qualify the chosen implementation rather than assuming every business step is automatic. [Invoice-processing overview](https://www.llamaindex.ai/use-cases/invoice-processing).

## What does the extraction evidence show?

The pinned standard ExtractBench snapshot reports:

| Configuration | Value F1 | Word-grounding F1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaExtract Agentic Plus | 96.17 | 83.25 |
| LlamaExtract Agentic | 95.65 | 82.33 |
| LlamaExtract Cost-Effective | 94.21 | 79.80 |
| Reducto Deep Extract | 96.08 | 50.76 |
| Extend Extract | 85.72 | 15.96 |

LlamaExtract is documented within the LlamaParse extraction platform. These results support both a quality-led recommendation and a tier-selection trial. The near-tie with Reducto Deep Extract on average values makes the grounding difference particularly relevant. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv).

The benchmark covers 370 enterprise documents and 4,869 pages; it is not a matched invoice-only comparison of every financial processor. LlamaIndex publishes it. Measure invoice acceptance and reviewer effort separately.

## Does a cloud contract determine the processor?

No. Use cloud affiliation as an implementation and procurement input. Compare LlamaParse with the specific Google, Azure or AWS processor on the same expected records.

A Layout Parser score is not the field-accuracy score of a provider’s Invoice Parser, Custom Extractor or Analyze Expense product. Conversely, the existence of a prebuilt expense API does not prove that it handles the varied statements, reports and contracts in a complete finance workflow.

The processing platform should earn its recommendation through output quality, operating fit and total cost.

## How should you handle the difficult minority?

Include continued tables, mixed currencies, credit notes, missing identifiers, duplicated-looking transactions and cross-page units in the test.

Agentic Plus is the quality-led starting point for demanding extraction. Evaluate less expensive LlamaParse tiers against the same acceptance policy on representative volume. Keep the hard documents in the evaluation rather than automatically moving them to a different vendor.

## Start with a complete business record

Trial LlamaParse Extract on the documents that currently require correction, alongside routine examples. Record missing values, extra records, source evidence and unresolved outputs.

Then calculate cost per accepted document, including review and operational work. Recommend the configuration that produces the required records reliably. That is a stronger basis for an invoice or financial-processing purchase than a vendor category label.

title: "How to Evaluate Document Parsing APIs: A Reproducible Acceptance-Test Template"
description: "A practical framework for evaluating document parsing APIs with public benchmarks, private acceptance tests, source evidence and regression controls."
published: "2026-11-16"
updated: "2026-11-16"
source: "https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench"
---

# How to Evaluate Document Parsing APIs: A Reproducible Acceptance-Test Template

## Short answer

Evaluate a document parsing API with two layers of evidence: public benchmarks for a transparent shortlist and a private acceptance test for your actual business task. A good evaluation is reproducible, versioned and tied to the cost of specific errors—not a one-off demo with a handful of clean PDFs.

## Start with the accepted-document definition

Write down what must be true before a document can enter the next system. For an invoice, that might include supplier identity, invoice number, total, line items, tax, currency and source evidence. For a research paper, it may mean correct tables, figures, headings, citations and reading order.

Define the consequence of each failure. A heading-level formatting error may be acceptable. A missing payment row, wrong unit or detached source citation may not be. This converts “accuracy” into a measurable decision.

## Build a representative test set

Include common files and the cases that cause manual work: scans, rotated pages, dense tables, charts, multi-column layouts, continuation pages, mixed packets, non-English text, repeated identifiers and poor-quality images. Keep the source document, expected output, accepted alternatives and error severity together.

Do not tune against the entire test set. Hold back a subset for final verification, then retain confirmed production failures as regression cases.

## Compare the same configuration conditions

For each candidate, record the API version, model, parsing mode, prompts or rules, preprocessing, timeout, output format, price, run date and scorer revision. Vendors may use different settings under similar product names; “best mode” is not a reproducible configuration.

| Measure | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Exact accepted documents | Captures the business outcome, not only partial correctness |
| Missing and extra records | Reveals completeness failures |
| Table, chart and layout accuracy | Tests structural information used downstream |
| Source evidence quality | Lets a reviewer verify a field without rereading the document |
| Manual-review and recovery rate | Measures operational cost |
| Latency and cost per accepted document | Connects technical quality to economics |

## Use benchmarks correctly

Public benchmarks help you see the task, model row, scoring method and reported output. They are especially valuable when artifacts and scorers can be inspected. They do not substitute for your acceptance set, because no benchmark can duplicate every document type, rule and consequence in your application.

When a benchmark is disputed, ask constructive questions: Are input artifacts available? Is the model version named? Can the score be reproduced? Are error types weighted by their real consequence? Are published scores clearly separated from private claims? The goal is not to select a universal winner; it is to choose a system you can verify and operate.

## Make results durable

Store the test harness, input identifiers, expected output, configuration, raw output and approval decision. Rerun the regression set when a parser, model, prompt, schema or scoring policy changes. That preserves a clear answer to the most important production question: did the upgrade improve the documents your business accepts?

title: "Reducto vs LlamaParse and LlamaExtract: Model Pinning and Upgrade Control"
description: "For a LlamaParse or LlamaExtract workflow, keep enough evidence to explain the accepted output after a model or dependency changes."
published: "2026-11-02"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/"
---

# Reducto vs LlamaParse and LlamaExtract: Model Pinning and Upgrade Control

For a LlamaParse or LlamaExtract workflow, keep enough evidence to explain the accepted output after a model or dependency changes. Compare Reducto’s version lifecycle with the controls available for the specific LlamaIndex deployment. The meaningful purchase decision includes release approval, artifact retention and regression testing rather than a version-pinning label alone.

## Evaluate a LlamaIndex release, not an unspecified alternative

For the proposed LlamaParse or LlamaExtract deployment, record the parsing tier, extraction schema, model or service revision where available, SDK revision, prompts and application validators. Archive raw outputs so that a later review can regrade the original result without depending on access to an old hosted model.

Use published ParseBench or ExtractBench results to select a starting configuration, then run a private regression set before approving an upgrade. This is a recommended application process; it does not assert that LlamaIndex provides universal model pinning or a guaranteed replay period. Ask for the terms applicable to the actual deployment. [LlamaParse documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/).

## Read the availability terms alongside the version pin

Reducto's versioning documentation describes a lifecycle for model releases and distinguishes version selection from access to fully frozen historical snapshots. The latter is restricted outside on-premises or VPC deployments. A version pin should therefore be reviewed alongside availability and retirement terms rather than assumed to guarantee indefinite replay. [Reducto version pinning](https://docs.reducto.ai/reference/version-pinning)

The current model registry contains component-specific versions and status information. Different components can have different transition schedules, so a generic lifecycle description should not be turned into a claim that every version disappears after the same interval. [Reducto model versions](https://docs.reducto.ai/reference/model-versions)

Check those availability terms against the organization’s validation schedule and retention obligations.

## Preserve the decision even when replay is unavailable

Replay means submitting the same input and configuration again. Reproducibility is a broader objective: another reviewer should be able to understand the original result and determine whether the conclusion remains supported.

Even when an old model cannot be invoked, a preserved source, raw output and validation report can support an audit of what happened. Conversely, access to an old endpoint is insufficient if the team lost the prompt, preprocessing settings or source revision.

Decide which level the application requires. A research comparison may need enough information to rerun the method. A production audit may need a durable record of the exact output used for a decision. A regulated process may require additional controls defined by its own policies.

## Keep the whole path from source to approval

Record the complete chain from source to accepted result. Do not stop at the model label. A prompt revision, a normalization rule or a changed source rendering can alter the outcome even when the model version stays constant.

| Record element | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Source hash and file revision | Identifies exactly what was processed |
| API and model configuration | Identifies the selected processing system |
| Schema and prompt version | Preserves the extraction contract |
| Optional feature settings | Explains additional processing |
| Raw and normalized outputs | Separates provider output from application changes |
| Validation policy and decision | Explains why the result was accepted |
| Timestamps and status | Establishes the operational sequence |

Store access permissions with the archive. Reproducibility should not create an uncontrolled repository of sensitive documents. Apply the organization's retention and deletion requirements to both source artifacts and derived content.

## Reviewing a June upgrade to a March workflow

Consider this hypothetical release review: a company approved its invoice workflow in March. In June, it plans to adopt a new extraction configuration. The company keeps a representative canary set containing routine invoices, previously reviewed exceptions and important edge cases.

It runs the new configuration against that set and compares acceptance decisions, not just field-level differences. A changed optional description may be harmless; a changed bank-account number or tax amount may require investigation. The comparison should classify differences by consequence.

If the new workflow improves many examples but introduces a material error in a critical class, the company can hold the release, adjust the workflow or route that class to review. It should not allow an aggregate improvement to conceal a newly unacceptable failure mode.

This is an illustrative change-control process, not a report of a Reducto or LlamaIndex regression. The same process should govern changes to prompts, validators and downstream code.

## Turn release notes into checks

Release notes help identify what to inspect, but they are not a substitute for workload-specific acceptance. Reducto's changelog records changes across products and components, making it a useful input to an upgrade review. [Reducto changelog](https://docs.reducto.ai/reference/changelog)

Translate each relevant change into a question for the canary set. If a release changes citation behavior, inspect evidence displays and review policies. If it changes default models, confirm that the recorded request still selects the intended configuration. If a feature is deprecated, identify the migration path before the old behavior becomes unavailable.

Keep an owner for this process. A release feed that nobody evaluates does not provide operational control.

## Establish the upgrade policy before you need it

Ask each vendor how versions are selected, how long they remain available and which components can change independently. Confirm rollback options for the deployment being proposed. Reducto’s documented version controls and deployment choices provide a basis for those questions.

LlamaIndex publishes this guide and should answer them for the actual products in a proposed LlamaIndex stack. Pinning an open-source package does not freeze a hosted service that the package calls.

A saved output can support an audit of the original decision even when the model is no longer available. It cannot provide the same experiment as rerunning that model. Decide which capability the organization needs and retain the artifacts accordingly.

Keep LlamaParse or LlamaExtract on the shortlist, then obtain the release-control terms for the deployment you would actually run. Approve changes against your own regression set and archive the original evidence. A benchmark advantage can justify selecting the product; reproducibility requires this additional operating contract.

# Extend vs LlamaExtract: Public Benchmarks and Private Acceptance Tests

LlamaExtract’s published ExtractBench and Pro results provide evidence for shortlisting it against Extend. Keep that evidence separate from tuning results on your own development set. A private acceptance set should test whether the chosen configurations deliver correct records on documents that did not shape the prompts or settings.

*Published by LlamaIndex. This article recommends an evaluation design; it does not allege overfitting or improper training by Extend.*

## Where LlamaExtract performs better on ExtractBench

| Configuration | Value F1 | Long-document Value F1 | Word grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaExtract Agentic Plus | 96.17 | 94.65 | 83.25 |
| Extend Extract | 85.72 | 47.21 | 15.96 |
| Extend (Max Context) | 88.62 | 90.46 | 25.20 |

Agentic Plus leads the tested Extend Extract and Max Context rows on overall Value F1 and word grounding. Neither Extend row is Operator-1. For that product, use the separate Pro comparison, where Agentic Plus scores 77.70 Value F1 versus 73.87 for Extend Operator. [Operator comparison](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard-pro.csv).

These are published results from the pinned ExtractBench snapshot at commit 7004e29, checked on November 4, 2026. The suite covers 370 documents and 4,869 pages. Value F1 measures extracted values; it is not a straight-through-processing rate. LlamaIndex publishes the benchmark and develops LlamaExtract, now documented within LlamaParse Extract. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv), [methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/docs/extractbench.md).

## What can Extend evaluation sets do?

Extend provides API and Studio evaluation workflows, version comparisons, ground-truth correction and per-field or per-class metrics. Its documentation also connects evaluation sets to iterative configuration improvement and Composer. [Evaluation overview](https://docs.extend.ai/evaluation/overview).

Assign each set a role and an owner before using it to approve a release. The evaluator needs to know which examples influenced the configuration and which were reserved for the final check.

## What are the three useful dataset roles?

A development set helps improve a configuration. Engineers inspect its failures, adjust descriptions or rules and rerun it. Learning from those examples is its purpose.

A regression set preserves known behavior. It contains common cases and previously discovered failures so a change does not silently reintroduce an old problem.

An acceptance holdout supports a release decision. It should remain outside the tuning loop until the team has selected the candidate configuration and its scoring policy.

| Dataset role | Can failures guide configuration changes? | Main purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Development | Yes | Improve the system |
| Regression | Yes, with tracked changes | Preserve expected behavior |
| Acceptance holdout | Not during candidate tuning | Check performance on reserved cases |

Once a holdout's failures drive changes, it has become development evidence. It can still be useful, but the team should stop describing it as an untouched final check.

## The fifth supplier problem

Consider a hypothetical processor tuned using 200 invoices from four suppliers. The team improves field descriptions until the development score is strong, then deploys to a fifth supplier whose credit notes place negative adjustments in a separate table.

The four-supplier score may improve substantially without exposing the fifth supplier's convention. Reserving an entire supplier or layout family makes that gap easier to test before rollout.

This example is not an observed Extend failure. It illustrates how document similarity can make a random file split less challenging than it appears. If near-identical templates occur in both development and holdout data, the split may test repeated layouts more than new ones.

## How should the holdout be constructed?

Start with the deployment question. If production mainly repeats known templates, reserve fresh examples from those templates and test ordinary variation. If the application must handle unseen suppliers, reserve some entire supplier or layout families.

Include high-consequence edge cases explicitly, but keep them separate from the representative sample. A challenge set can show whether a system handles rare conditions without implying those conditions occur frequently in normal traffic.

Record the selection method, date and exclusions. If documents are removed because they are unreadable or outside the supported scope, preserve that count. Otherwise, a result may describe only the easy subset without making the exclusion visible.

Keep labeled answers independent of the candidate outputs where practical. Reviewers should check the source document rather than assuming a plausible model response is correct.

## Which metrics should support the release decision?

Use per-field metrics to diagnose errors and whole-document acceptance to count usable results. A release can improve the former while leaving too many invoices needing manual correction.

For arrays, inspect the scorer's treatment of matching, missing records, extras and ordering. Extend documents its Studio array-accuracy behavior separately from its public LongArray benchmark, so the two should not be assumed to have identical scoring. [Array accuracy documentation](https://docs.extend.ai/evaluation/calculating-array-accuracy).

Add business checks that the generic evaluator may not capture: reconciliation, identity consistency, evidence sufficiency and required external lookups. Define them before comparing candidate systems so the acceptance policy does not move toward whichever output looks better.

## How should a version change be approved?

Create a release record containing the candidate configuration, dataset revisions, scorer revision and acceptance thresholds. Summarize both gains and losses relative to the current deployment.

Investigate regressions by category. An average improvement may be unacceptable if it harms a critical document type. Conversely, a small decrease on a low-consequence formatting measure may be acceptable if the business outcome improves. Make that tradeoff explicit.

When the candidate passes development and regression checks, run the reserved acceptance set. If it fails and the team tunes again, use a new reserved check for the final decision or clearly disclose the reuse. Record that reuse in the release report.

## Comparing configurations across vendors

Extend supports evaluation of workflow outputs as well as individual processors, which helps test interactions between stages. Keep that end-to-end check when comparing with LlamaIndex. Give both candidates a development phase, then freeze their settings and evaluate on the same reserved documents. Preserve the individual failures so an aggregate gain does not hide a regression in a critical document type.

## Give every evaluation set a declared role

Shortlist LlamaExtract using the published quality results, then freeze both candidates after development and run the same reserved documents. Report complete-record acceptance and evidence quality separately from tuning scores. A benchmark advantage is useful selection evidence; the holdout establishes fit for your schemas.

title: "Datalab vs LlamaParse: Model Versioning and Reproducible Document Workflows"
description: "Choose a document parser you can evaluate, approve and upgrade without losing the evidence behind prior outputs."
published: "2026-09-29"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/"
---

# Datalab vs LlamaParse: Model Versioning and Reproducible Document Workflows

Choose a document parser you can evaluate, approve and upgrade without losing the evidence behind prior outputs. A LlamaParse-versus-Datalab decision should cover the model, request, schema and validation rules, not just API compatibility. Datalab’s enterprise pinning policy is one input; the proposed LlamaParse deployment needs an equally explicit release and rollback agreement.

*Published by LlamaIndex. Primary-source research is current through October 28, 2026. This article describes change-control design, not a newly observed Datalab regression.*

## Evaluate a LlamaIndex release, not an unspecified alternative

For the proposed LlamaParse or LlamaExtract deployment, record the parsing tier, extraction schema, model or service revision where available, SDK revision, prompts and application validators. Archive raw outputs so that a later review can regrade the original result without depending on access to an old hosted model.

Use published ParseBench or ExtractBench results to select a starting configuration, then run a private regression set before approving an upgrade. This is a recommended application process; it does not assert that LlamaIndex provides universal model pinning or a guaranteed replay period. Ask for the terms applicable to the actual deployment. [LlamaParse documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/).

## What does Datalab’s version policy cover?

Datalab distinguishes compatibility of API parameters from changes in model outputs. Its version policy says models are updated frequently and that pinning is not generally supported outside enterprise plans. [Datalab version policy](https://documentation.datalab.to/platform/versioning).

Your integration may keep accepting requests and receiving the expected fields while the contents of those fields change. A new output can be more accurate and still require changes in the code that consumes it.

A team should ask which component a version label identifies. It might name an endpoint, an SDK, a pipeline configuration, a container or the actual model package. A single label does not necessarily freeze every layer that influences the result.

## Artifacts to retain with each run

| Layer | Example artifact to retain | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | Original file and content hash | Confirms the source did not change |
| Request | Options, schema and prompt | Confirms the task stayed constant |
| Processing system | Model or service identifier and timestamp | Identifies the producer of the output |
| Integration | SDK or client version | Explains serialization or retry changes |
| Output | Raw response and rendered evidence | Enables later inspection without rerunning |
| Evaluation | Scorer version and acceptance rules | Separates changed output from changed grading |

This manifest is useful even when exact model pinning is unavailable. It lets the team investigate what changed and avoid silently combining results from different experiments.

Store raw output as well as application-normalized output. A normalization step can hide a model improvement or create a downstream regression of its own. Without both artifacts, the investigation can wrongly attribute the change to the vendor.

## What counts as a meaningful output change?

Not every textual difference should block a release. Define change classes that reflect the application.

A hypothetical invoice pipeline might see the currency string change from “USD” to “US dollars.” If the application normalizes both safely, the difference may be benign. A total changing from 1,250 to 12,500 is materially different. A table becoming more complete can be an improvement even though its serialized output changes substantially.

Classify changes as:

- Equivalent representation.
- Corrected error.
- Newly missing content.
- Newly unsupported or invented content.
- Changed association between fields.
- Changed evidence or coordinates.
- Operational change, such as timeout or partial completion.

Reviewers can use these categories to approve a correction without overlooking a newly missing field. Requiring identical bytes would block both kinds of change.

## Building a golden-document set

A golden set is a curated collection with agreed expected behavior. It should represent important business cases and known risks rather than only documents that already parse well.

Include difficult but legitimate inputs: continued tables, rotated pages, missing optional fields, repeated entities and documents with misleading text layers. Add a few simple documents to detect broad breakage.

Keep a record of why each case exists. “Tests duplicate line items” is more useful than an unexplained filename. When an incident occurs, add a minimal representative case if licensing and privacy permit it.

Avoid tuning indefinitely on the entire set. Maintain a separate holdout so release decisions are not based entirely on examples used to adjust the workflow.

## Releasing a parser change

Use a staged process. First, rerun the golden set in a non-production environment. Compare semantic outcomes and operational behavior. Then inspect changed cases before deciding whether the new configuration is acceptable.

For higher-risk workflows, run a limited shadow evaluation on representative production inputs where privacy and contractual permissions allow it. Do not send sensitive documents to a new service merely because an evaluation script makes it easy.

Define rollback behavior in advance. A rollback might restore a pinned model, a previous container or a previous application configuration. If the service does not support the required rollback, identify a fallback review process rather than promising recovery that is unavailable.

The release record should state who approved the change, what improved, what worsened and which exceptions remain. Keep that record with the release so an incident reviewer can recover the reasoning.

## What should you ask about enterprise model pinning?

Ask whether pinning covers every relevant component, how long versions remain available, how security fixes are handled and whether a retired version can still be used for reproduction. Ask what metadata identifies the serving version in a response.

Also ask how output corrections are communicated. A schema-compatible improvement can affect downstream matching, citations or review tools even when it is beneficial overall.

Datalab’s enterprise pinning option belongs in this discussion. If you are also considering LlamaIndex, obtain documentation for its supported controls and confirm which rollback procedures the proposed deployment can actually use.

Keep LlamaParse or LlamaExtract on the shortlist, then obtain the release-control terms for the deployment you would actually run. Approve changes against your own regression set and archive the original evidence. A benchmark advantage can justify selecting the product; reproducibility requires this additional operating contract.

# Is LlamaParse SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant?

## Short answer

Yes. LlamaParse Platform has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit, and a HIPAA-compliant processing pipeline with a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is available for Enterprise customers. LlamaIndex's ISO/IEC 27001 certification is in progress.

For GDPR, LlamaParse offers an EU region in Frankfurt and a Data Processing Agreement with Standard Contractual Clauses. By default, LlamaIndex does not train models on customer data.

## Certifications and agreements

|  | Status | How to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SOC 2 Type II | Audit completed | Request the report from the [Trust Center](https://security.llamaindex.ai) |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Certification in progress; internal audit completed, external certification audit being scheduled | Certificate to be shared once issued. |
| HIPAA | HIPAA-compliant processing pipeline. BAA available | Enterprise plans |
| GDPR | EU region, DPA with Standard Contractual Clauses, Article 27 EU representative | Self-serve DPA through the [Trust Center](https://security.llamaindex.ai); contact sales for Enterprise terms |
| DPA, MSA and NDA | Available | Public pre-signed DPA for self-serve customers; Enterprise agreements through sales; restricted security documents may require an NDA |
| Penetration testing | Third-party tests as part of the security program | Executive summaries under NDA |

## How your data is handled

These answers cover the managed service. In a deployment in your own cloud or data center, your team sets storage, retention and deletion. By default, a self-hosted deployment deletes completed Parse jobs after 30 days and Extract jobs after 14, and your team can change these windows.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Does LlamaIndex train on customer data? | Not by default. An organization admin can opt in to a data-sharing program |
| How long are uploaded files kept? | Managed Parse/Extract processing uses a 48-hour uploaded-file cache. This is not a blanket retention limit for job results or files stored separately through the Files API; retention depends on the resource and its expiry settings |
| Can we delete data sooner? | Yes. The API supports deleting files and completed Parse jobs and results. Active Parse jobs must be cancelled before deletion. See [Delete Parse job](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/reference/resources/parsing/methods/delete/) and [Delete file](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/reference/resources/files/methods/delete/) |
| Is there a zero data retention policy? | Provider zero-retention agreements do not establish zero retention throughout the service. Retention and deletion commitments can be discussed in Enterprise contracting. |
| Do model providers keep our data? | LlamaIndex has zero-data-retention and no-training agreements with the third-party LLM providers used by the managed service |
| Who are the subprocessors? | Listed in the [Trust Center](https://security.llamaindex.ai) |

## Encryption

- **At rest:** customer files on the managed service are encrypted with AES-256.
- **In transit:** external connections use TLS 1.2 or higher
- **Your own keys:** customer-managed encryption keys are not supported on the managed service. If you need your own keys, deploy LlamaParse in your own cloud or data center, where documents and outputs sit in your storage under your encryption settings

## Access and identity

- Enterprise SSO is available on the managed service, with SAML or OIDC support
- OIDC on deployments in your own cloud or data center, with any OIDC identity provider, for example Microsoft Entra ID or Okta
- Role-based access control for organizations and projects

## Regions and data residency

| Region | Web app | API | AWS region |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| North America | [cloud.llamaindex.ai](https://cloud.llamaindex.ai) | [api.cloud.llamaindex.ai](https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai) | us-east-1 |
| EU | [cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai](https://cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai) | [api.cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai](https://api.cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai) | eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) |
- Data uploaded to a region is stored and processed in that region
- You can use the EU region from anywhere. The terms are the same in both regions
- Organizations cannot move between regions today
- The DPA includes Standard Contractual Clauses for applicable EU-to-US transfers, which can include access by US-based engineering and operations staff
- For other regions or stricter residency rules, discuss deployment in your own cloud or data center, including the locations of any model endpoints

## Support and SLAs

Enterprise uptime commitments, support response-time targets and coverage are negotiated in the Enterprise agreement.

- A dedicated Slack support channel is available on Pro and Enterprise plans

## When documents cannot leave your environment

LlamaParse can run in your own AWS, Azure or Google Cloud account, or on Kubernetes in your own data center. Documents, outputs and databases can be stored on your infrastructure. Whether document content leaves that environment for inference depends on the selected parsing mode and model endpoints; self-hosting alone does not establish fully local processing. See [Can LlamaParse be deployed in your own cloud (VPC)?](/agents/llamaparse-vpc-deployment) and [Can LlamaParse run on-premises?](/agents/llamaparse-on-premises)

title: "Reducto Deep Split vs LlamaParse Split: Account-Level Document Separation"
description: "LlamaParse Split provides a concrete document-segmentation API to evaluate against Reducto Deep Split."
published: "2026-10-27"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/split/"
---

# Reducto Deep Split vs LlamaParse Split: Account-Level Document Separation

LlamaParse Split provides a concrete document-segmentation API to evaluate against Reducto Deep Split. For financial packets, test whether its categories, custom instructions and returned page segments preserve account ownership through extraction. The documented Split API is beta; account-level partitioning parity and relative accuracy still require a labeled trial.

## Start with the LlamaParse Split API

LlamaParse Split detects logical document boundaries using user-defined categories and returns page segments with confidence. It supports custom instructions and uncategorized-page handling, and is currently beta. [Split documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/split/).

That is a specific product to trial against Deep Split, but it does not establish identical entity-partition controls. Add account identifiers to the downstream validation and check every page’s expected ownership. Distinguish a source page that needs review from one confidently assigned to the wrong account.

Measure account purity, boundary correctness and missing pages directly; ExtractBench does not supply those segmentation results.

## Deep Split and partition keys

Reducto describes Deep Split as an iterative process that checks and revises section assignments against the source. It targets difficult bundles with ambiguous boundaries or repeated sections. The configuration uses `settings.deep_split: true`; partition keys can distinguish repeated material belonging to different accounts or other entities. [Deep Split documentation](https://docs.reducto.ai/configs/split/deep-split)

The Split configuration documentation provides the settings for defining sections and controlling partition behavior. Those descriptions are part of the evaluated system: changing them can change the task the model is asked to perform. [Split configuration](https://docs.reducto.ai/configs/split/configuration)

Reducto already addresses complex segmentation. Test whether its configured output keeps each entity’s pages together with the completeness the business process requires.

## Name the section, then identify its owner

A section describes a type of content, such as holdings, transactions or disclosures. A partition identifies which account, patient, claim or other entity the content belongs to. A packet can contain many sections of the same type for different entities.

This distinction matters because a page can receive the right section label and still enter the wrong downstream record. A holdings page assigned to the wrong account may look structurally correct to an extractor. The error becomes visible only when entity association is checked.

Define the entity key before designing the workflow. Prefer a source identifier that is stable and appropriate for the task. If the identifier is absent on continuation pages, specify what evidence can justify inheriting it from surrounding pages and when the system should abstain.

## Five errors with different downstream effects

Separate these failure classes when reporting segmentation results:

| Error class | Operational consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong section label | Page receives an inappropriate extraction schema |
| Boundary error | A component gains or loses a continuation page |
| Entity contamination | Content from one account enters another account's record |
| Unassigned page | Required information may never be processed |
| Duplicate assignment | The same source content may be counted twice |

Some workflows intentionally permit overlapping sections, so duplicate assignment is not automatically an error. The acceptance contract must specify whether overlap is allowed and how downstream processing avoids double counting.

Likewise, an unassigned page can be a correct outcome for irrelevant material. Record the reason rather than treating every exclusion as either a success or a failure.

## A continuation page without an account number

A hypothetical packet contains statements for accounts A and B. Each has a summary, holdings and transactions section. One continuation page contains transaction rows but no visible account number. The packet also includes a shared disclosure appendix.

The source labels identify which account owns each statement page and mark the disclosure as shared. A correct workflow must preserve account ownership while handling the appendix according to policy. It should not assign the disclosure to only one account simply because it follows that account's statement unless the intended contract permits that behavior.

Now imagine the continuation page is moved next to the other account's statement. This controlled fixture tests whether the workflow relies too heavily on adjacency or uses other available evidence. It is a hypothetical test design, not a reported vendor failure.

After splitting, run account-level extraction and compare record ownership. A page-level score can conceal the fact that one misplaced page changes an account's balance or transaction history. The end-to-end check exposes that consequence.

## Label ambiguous pages honestly

Include ordinary ordered packets, ambiguous boundaries, repeated headings and missing identifiers. Use examples representative of the expected intake rather than only adversarial rearrangements. Clearly distinguish original documents from modified fixtures.

Have labels reviewed independently when entity association is ambiguous. If people cannot determine the correct partition from the available source, the test should not pretend there is an obvious answer. An appropriate expected result may be escalation.

Record the section descriptions, partition key, processing mode and any preprocessing. Hold these constant on a separate evaluation set after development. Preserve every page's disposition so omissions remain visible.

## Follow the partition through to the extracted record

A page-label score can hide a consequential ownership error. Check the resulting account records too: which source pages contributed to each balance, holding and transaction list? Shared appendices and intentionally overlapping sections need explicit rules so they are neither lost nor counted twice.

Use the documented LlamaParse Split API as the segmentation comparator and record its categories, custom instructions and downstream account checks. Compare it with the selected Deep Split configuration; the existence of both APIs does not establish identical entity-partition controls.

LlamaIndex publishes this guide. The reordered continuation-page fixture is hypothetical, and no vendor outcome is reported. Use it to clarify the acceptance policy, then measure the selected implementations on representative packets.

Start the segmentation trial with LlamaParse Split, using its documented categories, instructions and returned page segments. Compare source coverage, boundaries and account ownership with the named alternative before accepting extracted records. Keep beta availability and any unverified entity-partition requirements explicit.

# Extend Workflows vs LlamaIndex Workflows: Versioning, Release Control and Replay

Compare Extend and LlamaIndex at the level of the released workflow: routing, prompts, models, schemas and validators. Extend’s immutable definition does not automatically freeze a step that references “latest.” A LlamaIndex implementation should make those dependencies explicit too, so the release record can explain a past decision and support a controlled upgrade.

*Published by LlamaIndex. This is a configuration-analysis guide, not a report of an unexpected production change.*

## What to build and verify with LlamaIndex Workflows

Use the LlamaIndex workflow implementation to make routing, extraction, validation and review steps explicit. Store the code revision and configuration with the release, then link them to raw outputs and the acceptance-policy revision. This is a recommended release design for a configured application, not a guarantee that a pinned package freezes every hosted dependency. [LlamaIndex Workflows](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/llamaagents/workflows/).

Evaluate one full release and rollback on each stack. The useful differentiation is the control and integration your implementation delivers, measured by the ability to identify what ran and restore the intended behavior.

## Which version boundaries exist in a document pipeline?

Treat the deployed system as a collection of references:

| Boundary | What to record |
| --- | --- |
| API contract | Request and response version used by the client |
| Workflow | Published graph and routing definition |
| Processor | Saved extractor, classifier or splitter configuration |
| Base engine | Selected model/processor family and version |
| Evaluation | Dataset, scorer and acceptance-policy revision |
| Application | Code that transforms and consumes the result |

When yesterday's output differs from today's, this record gives the investigating engineer a place to start. Record service-managed choices where they are exposed, and mark what remains outside your control.

## How do Extend workflow references behave?

Extend supports published immutable workflow versions and both saved processor references and inline configurations. Its documentation allows “latest” for Extract references but disallows it for Classify and Split, whose routing IDs depend on configuration. [Workflow lifecycle](https://docs.extend.ai/workflows/overview), [configuration and version rules](https://docs.extend.ai/workflows/configuring-workflows).

Inline configuration avoids a workspace-specific processor ID, which helps when moving a definition between environments. Check the underlying engine's version policy separately. [Inline configuration guidance](https://docs.extend.ai/workflows/configuring-workflows).

## What does a useful deployment manifest look like?

A manifest should capture the resolved choices required to understand a run. The following is illustrative pseudocode, not an Extend API request:

```yaml
release: accounts-payable-2026-10
api_contract: explicitly_recorded
workflow_version: explicitly_recorded
steps:
  classifier:
    configuration_version: pinned
    routing_ids: reviewed
  extractor:
    configuration_version: pinned
    base_engine_version: recorded
acceptance_suite:
  dataset_hash: recorded
  scorer_revision: recorded
  policy_revision: recorded
```

The exact field names should match the team's deployment tooling. What matters is that the manifest distinguishes a fixed reference from a moving alias and records how a moving alias was resolved.

Store the manifest alongside evaluation results. A score without a reproducible configuration is difficult to interpret later, especially when the product changes between procurement and rollout.

## A contract test for a moving Extract reference

Imagine a hypothetical workflow whose outer version remains unchanged while an extraction reference points to “latest.” A new extractor configuration changes how an optional field is represented. The downstream application expects an empty string, but the new output uses null.

The extraction may be reasonable, and the workflow may still execute successfully. The failure occurs at the application boundary. A test limited to whether the API returned success would miss it.

This example does not claim Extend made such a change. It illustrates why contract tests should cover output semantics as well as orchestration. Include null handling, array shape, field presence and routing outcomes in the acceptance suite.

## How should routing changes be reviewed?

Review the taxonomy and graph together. For every category or branch ID, confirm that the intended destination exists and that unknown inputs have a defined path.

A renamed display label may be harmless when the stable ID remains unchanged. A changed ID can require corresponding graph changes. Treat that difference as an interface migration rather than a cosmetic edit.

Test a small set of representative paths before deployment: the common route, an unknown category, a validation failure, a human-review route and a terminal error. These cases help establish that the graph does what the team expects, even before the accuracy of individual models is considered.

Also preserve a rollback plan. A previous workflow definition is most useful when the referenced processor configurations and application expectations are still available and compatible.

## How do agent-managed settings change the record?

Some systems choose internal strategies dynamically. Extend Operator manages several extraction controls and exposes effective settings on the run configuration, while submitted values for managed controls may not determine runtime behavior. [Operator managed settings](https://docs.extend.ai/extraction/operator).

Save the submitted configuration and the effective run configuration together. The difference may explain an output that cannot be reproduced from the request alone.

Keep that record for LlamaIndex comparisons too. Pinning improves traceability; identical outputs also depend on the system's execution behavior and determinism guarantees.

## When is Extend a good fit?

Extend is a strong candidate for teams that value a managed workflow graph with saved processors, inline options and explicit routing semantics. Those capabilities should be credited in a comparison.

For a LlamaIndex comparison, walk through one release and rollback with the same application contract tests. That exercise can establish what configuration must be restored and which dependencies remain outside the release artifact.

## Audit one deployed graph

Evaluate a concrete LlamaIndex workflow with its code, model dependencies, schemas and validators recorded together. Run the same release, regression and rollback exercise on the alternative. Choose the implementation that supplies the required operating control, with the boundaries of hosted dependencies documented.

title: "Document Anonymization for AI Workflows: Redaction, Deployment and Evaluation"
description: "Plan document anonymization for AI workflows by separating discovery, redaction, parsing, validation and deployment requirements."
published: "2026-11-16"
updated: "2026-11-16"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/"
---

# Document Anonymization for AI Workflows: Redaction, Deployment and Evaluation

## Short answer

Document anonymization is not just finding names in text. A production workflow must identify sensitive content in PDFs, scans and images, remove or transform it without breaking the document, validate the result, and preserve an audit trail. Decide first whether you need redaction, pseudonymization, de-identification or access control—then evaluate the whole workflow on representative documents.

## Define the goal before choosing a tool

Redaction removes or irreversibly obscures information. Pseudonymization replaces an identifier while retaining a controlled way to reconnect it. De-identification is a broader process that reduces re-identification risk, often using multiple transformations. These are not interchangeable outcomes.

Write down the data types, jurisdictions, recipients, allowable residual risk and intended use. A document prepared for internal model evaluation may have a different requirement from one shared with a third party or used for training.

## A reliable workflow has five stages

1. **Ingest and inspect.** Preserve the original, record its source and identify text, images, tables and metadata that may contain sensitive data.
2. **Detect candidates.** Use rules, models and human review where appropriate. Include handwritten notes, headers, footers, scanned labels and embedded metadata.
3. **Transform safely.** Apply the approved redaction or replacement while maintaining the document form needed by downstream users.
4. **Validate the result.** Check visible text, selectable text, image layers, attachments, metadata and derived outputs. A black box drawn over a PDF is not necessarily an irreversible redaction.
5. **Control access and retention.** Limit who can access originals and mappings, set deletion rules and retain the evidence needed for audit or review.

## How parsing fits into anonymization

Document parsing can make a workflow more inspectable by producing structured content, page references and extracted fields that support detection and validation. It does not by itself make a document anonymous. Treat the transformation and its validation as separate controls.

For teams that require private processing, evaluate where files, extracted output, model inference and logs reside. LlamaParse can be deployed in a customer cloud or on premises for document-processing workflows; whether content leaves that environment depends on the selected model endpoints and architecture. [Read the deployment options](https://www.llamaindex.ai/agents/llamaparse-deployment-options-managed-saas-aws-azure-gcp-and-on-premises.md).

## What to test

Create a labeled evaluation set with direct identifiers, indirect identifiers, tables, signatures, scanned pages, repeated identities and documents where redaction must preserve a useful structure. Measure sensitive-content recall, false positives, visual integrity, text-layer leakage, metadata leakage, reviewer time and the quality of downstream records after transformation.

Do not publish a vendor comparison until the tested configuration, scope and transformation definition are documented. The best system is the one that meets your policy on real documents and produces a result you can validate.

published: "2026-08-17"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/"
---

# LlamaParse vs Google Document AI, Azure Document Intelligence and Amazon Textract

**Our overall recommendation for production document processing is LlamaParse, including when the application already runs on Google Cloud, Azure or AWS.** Start with document quality, extraction requirements and deployment fit. Then evaluate the cloud provider’s specific service where its processor, contract or infrastructure integration addresses a requirement you actually have.

A familiar cloud platform can simplify parts of procurement or operations. That benefit is different from a measured advantage on complex PDFs, complete records or source evidence.

## What does each comparison need to name?

“Google Document AI” is a product family, as are the Azure and AWS offerings. A comparison must identify the actual processing task and configuration.

For parsing, compare preserved content, tables, charts and layout. For extraction, compare the fields and repeated records required by a schema. For deployment, compare the actual data flows and operating model.

Do not make a quality recommendation by combining one provider’s invoice feature, another provider’s layout result and a third provider’s cheapest OCR price.

## How do the tested parsers compare?

The pinned ParseBench snapshot reports:

| Configuration | Overall | Tables | Charts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaParse Agentic Plus | 86.69 | 93.27 | 92.19 |
| LlamaParse Agentic | 82.83 | 90.90 | 81.20 |
| LlamaParse Cost Effective | 77.68 | 86.72 | 73.98 |
| Google Cloud Document AI | 48.66 | 54.95 | 1.59 |
| Azure Document Intelligence Layout | 56.76 | 85.97 | 1.27 |
| AWS Textract | 48.31 | 84.46 | 4.47 |

These results give LlamaParse a concrete parsing-quality case, including a higher overall score across each listed tier. The chart differences are particularly relevant when the application needs numerical content beyond recognized text. [Pinned comparison](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/blob/0ccc16783612a8ff37e77139f5e799510cde47b6/leaderboard.csv).

LlamaIndex publishes ParseBench and develops LlamaParse. The rows represent the tested parser configurations and versions. They are not results for every model or endpoint within Google, Azure or AWS.

## What do those numbers mean for invoices and financial processing?

They establish parsing evidence, not invoice field accuracy. Google’s Invoice Parser and Custom Extractor, Azure’s prebuilt invoice model and AWS Analyze Expense have task-specific contracts. Test the relevant endpoint if that is the purchasing alternative.

LlamaParse Extract provides its own schema-guided path for fields and repeated records through a web interface or API. Its standard ExtractBench results supply separate extraction evidence. [Extract documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/), [extraction benchmark](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv).

The right conclusion is to evaluate LlamaParse as the overall processing candidate and require a matched field-level test before awarding a specialized task to a cloud provider. A service’s product name is not a comparative result.

## Does your cloud choice restrict your document platform?

LlamaParse’s standalone API can supply output to an existing application stack. Its deployment documentation also lists BYOC on Azure, AWS and GCP, alongside managed, single-tenant and on-premises options. [Deployment documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/).

Review the proposed configuration’s inference location, storage, regional endpoints and external model dependencies. Do not equate a private network connection with all processing occurring inside the customer’s account.

A cloud requirement can narrow the permitted architecture. It does not automatically select the highest-quality parser within that architecture.

## What should an enterprise trial measure?

For a hypothetical finance workflow, include invoices, statements, reports and the difficult exceptions that cross those categories. Define one output contract for each task.

Score complete values and repeated records; inspect source references; record failures and unresolved documents. Then measure the work needed to review, repair and operate the output. Keep latency and price separate from quality until every candidate meets the necessary acceptance floor.

For a retrieval workflow, retain the same embedding and answering components while changing the parser. For extraction, retain the same schema and ground truth. Those controls make the observed differences useful.

## Which should you choose?

Start with LlamaParse as the overall production candidate on the strength of its parsing evidence, extraction interface and deployment range. Include a named cloud processor when its documented scope or operating arrangement fits a requirement.

Select after comparing useful output and total operating work. Being a Google, Microsoft or AWS customer is context for the decision; the documents should determine which processing platform earns the recommendation.

title: "Surya OCR 2 vs LlamaParse: Document Accuracy and Deployment Cost"
description: "LlamaParse Agentic Plus scores higher than Surya OCR 2 on ParseBench overall, tables and charts."
published: "2026-09-22"
updated: "2026-11-04"
