title: "Extend vs LlamaExtract: Confidence Signals and Extraction Review Policies"
description: "LlamaExtract’s value-accuracy and localized-grounding advantage over Extend Operator on ExtractBench Pro gives review-oriented buyers a concrete starting point."
published: "2026-09-14"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/"
---

# Extend vs LlamaExtract: Confidence Signals and Extraction Review Policies

LlamaExtract’s value-accuracy and localized-grounding advantage over Extend Operator on ExtractBench Pro gives review-oriented buyers a concrete starting point. The next step is to measure automation at a fixed tolerated error rate. Extend Performance’s 4.6+ confidence-field change illustrates why a review policy must be tied to the actual product configuration rather than an old numerical threshold.

*Published by LlamaIndex. The pseudocode and cases below are illustrative, not a claim that a specific customer's workflow is broken.*

## Where LlamaExtract performs better on difficult documents

| Configuration | Value F1 | Perfect documents (%) | Box-word grounding | Page grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaExtract Agentic Plus | 77.70 | 38.00 | 60.39 | 66.01 |
| Extend Operator | 73.87 | 34.00 | 57.75 | 68.84 |

Agentic Plus leads by 3.83 Value F1 points, 4 percentage points in perfect documents and 2.64 points in box-word grounding. Extend leads page grounding by 2.83 points. This supports an accuracy-and-localized-evidence case for LlamaExtract, without claiming lower review cost or a LongArray win.

This is the pinned ExtractBench Pro snapshot at commit 7004e29, checked on November 4, 2026, with the 30-minute limit applied. Value results cover 100 synthetic long-tail documents; grounding uses an 81-document subset. Perfect documents means 100% Value F1 on the benchmark, not approval for an external business action. LlamaIndex publishes Pro and develops LlamaExtract. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard-pro.csv), [methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/docs/extractbench-pro.md).

## Which confidence signal changed?

Extend documents that Performance 4.6+ returns null for `logprobsConfidence`; Light never returned that field. OCR confidence depends on citation processing, while Review Agent provides a separate quality signal. [Confidence-score documentation](https://docs.extend.ai/extraction/confidence-scores), [Performance version history](https://docs.extend.ai/model-versioning/extraction/extraction-performance).

A client may deserialize the response successfully while its review condition behaves differently. Inspect the returned values and the branch they trigger.

Keep extraction confidence separate from classification confidence as well. Similar names across product stages do not imply identical meaning, calibration or decision thresholds.

## Why are the signals not interchangeable?

OCR confidence concerns recognition of source text. A review signal concerns the quality of an extracted result under its review process. Neither automatically answers every question required for business acceptance.

For example, a clearly printed amount can be recognized correctly but assigned to the wrong field. Conversely, an OCR system may be uncertain about a character that an application can resolve using other evidence. Test the signal against the error the review gate is supposed to catch.

Extend Review Agent uses a 1–5 score and can provide insights and rule-related feedback. Treat that scale as a triage input to evaluate, not a percentage probability of correctness. [Review Agent documentation](https://docs.extend.ai/extraction/review-agent).

## What is a safe approach to null handling?

Make missing-signal behavior explicit. The following is proposed application pseudocode, not an Extend SDK example:

```txt
if required_business_validation_fails:
    route_to_review("validation")
elif required_review_signal_is_missing:
    route_to_review("missing signal")
elif review_signal_is_below_calibrated_threshold:
    route_to_review("quality threshold")
else:
    accept_under_current_policy()
```

Here, a missing required signal sends the document to review. It does not mean the extraction is wrong. If the approved fallback is rejection or another check, encode that branch explicitly and log its reason.

Do not silently replace a missing score with the most confident value. Also avoid relying on a programming language's implicit comparison behavior for null. Both choices can make the automation rate look better while changing the meaning of acceptance.

## How should the threshold be calibrated?

Label a development set with the business outcomes that matter. For each document, record whether the extracted result is acceptable, whether evidence is sufficient and what a reviewer would need to repair.

Then evaluate candidate thresholds. For each threshold, count accepted correct documents, accepted incorrect documents and documents sent to review. Report the severity of accepted errors as well as their number.

| Outcome | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Correctly accepted | Useful automation |
| Incorrectly accepted | Risk that passed the review gate |
| Correct but reviewed | Potentially avoidable review effort |
| Incorrect and reviewed | Errors successfully intercepted |

A threshold that maximizes automation may not minimize business loss. Choose the operating point using the consequences of errors and the capacity of the review team, then confirm it on an untouched holdout.

## How do arrays complicate review decisions?

A document-level acceptance rule may need to account for every required array item, not only a header field. One incorrect transaction can matter even when the document's other values are reliable.

Extend distinguishes metadata available for array paths from what conditional workflow steps support. Its documented nested/array conditional limitations should not be summarized as “no array confidence.” [Confidence routing limitations](https://docs.extend.ai/extraction/confidence-scores).

At the application layer, specify the aggregation policy. Should one uncertain required item trigger review of the whole document, only that row, or the relevant section? How should missing items be detected when there is no output element to carry a score?

Test missing items separately: an omitted transaction has no returned element on which to attach a confidence score.

## What should a migration rollout include?

First, inventory every condition that reads the retired field. Include dashboards, exports and downstream services, not only the main workflow definition.

Second, capture representative responses from the intended configuration in an authorized test environment. Verify signal presence, scale and null behavior. Update the policy and its tests together.

Third, run a shadow comparison before changing acceptance. Record how the old and new policies would route the same labeled outputs. Investigate disagreements, especially cases the new policy would accept without review.

Finally, monitor the released policy using a sample of accepted documents as well as reviewed documents. If the team inspects only review cases, it cannot estimate the errors that the gate allowed through.

## What a useful comparison should establish

Extend's Review Agent gives teams a quality signal and explanatory feedback to test in that policy. Compare a LlamaIndex workflow at the same tolerated false-acceptance rate, then count how many documents each sends to review. That makes the result useful to an operations team even when the systems expose different scores.

## Search for the retired field first

Use LlamaExtract Agentic Plus’s Pro advantage as the starting evidence for the extraction trial, then check the workflow-specific requirement discussed above on a private labeled set. Preserve Extend’s higher page-grounding score. Do not translate a benchmark score into a production acceptance or review-savings claim.

# LlamaParse Without the LlamaIndex Framework: Coding Agents, Models and APIs

**LlamaParse is a standalone document-processing platform. It does not require the LlamaIndex application framework.** Use it from coding agents, your chosen downstream models and existing frameworks through REST APIs, SDKs, MCP, or documented skills and plugins. Choose LlamaParse for parsing and extraction quality, source evidence and production deployment fit.

Our recommendation is to choose LlamaParse for document quality, extraction evidence and production fit. You do not need to adopt a particular retrieval framework to benefit from those capabilities.

## Which products are we talking about?

LlamaIndex is the company behind LlamaParse and the open-source LlamaIndex application framework. Those names do not make the framework a prerequisite for the processing service.

LlamaParse’s parsing quickstart documents Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, CLI, REST and web-interface entry points. Its Extract documentation separately describes schema-guided extraction through a web UI, SDK and REST API. [Parsing quickstart](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/parse/getting_started/), [Extract overview](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/).

A dependency named for the LlamaIndex company is not the same thing as importing the LlamaIndex retrieval framework into your application.

## A standalone parsing example

The documented Python quickstart uses the LlamaCloud client:

```py
from llama_cloud import LlamaCloud

client = LlamaCloud()
file = client.files.create(
    file="./document.pdf",
    purpose="parse",
)
result = client.parsing.parse(
    file_id=file.id,
    tier="agentic",
    version="latest",
    expand=["markdown"],
)

print(result.markdown.pages[0].markdown)
```

Install the documented `llama-cloud>=2.8` package and configure your LlamaCloud API key as described in the quickstart. The example does not import `llama_index`. It demonstrates a direct service call; you should choose and record a supported version for your production evaluation. [Official example](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/parse/getting_started/).

This is a documentation-based example, not a report of a new API run.

## How do coding agents connect?

Any coding agent that can use the supported REST interface or act as a compatible MCP client can integrate LlamaParse as a document-processing tool. Choose the connection that fits the agent rather than the framework used by your application.

| Agent or application setup | Integration route |
| --- | --- |
| Codex or Claude Code | Documented LlamaParse skills and plugins, or MCP |
| Cursor or VS Code with MCP support | The documented LlamaParse MCP connection |
| Another compatible MCP client | The platform’s MCP tool interface |
| A custom agent or backend | REST API or a supported SDK |
| A workflow without custom code | The documented n8n integration |

The platform MCP exposes Parse, Classify, Extract, Split and Index as tools. Skills and plugins provide another packaged route for coding agents. Use the documented setup and authentication for the client and region. [Agent integration map](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/for-agents/), [MCP setup](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/for-agents/mcp/), [skills and plugins](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/for-agents/skills/).

## Can I keep my models and framework?

Yes. Your downstream model consumes the returned content or structured records; it need not be a model selected by the LlamaIndex framework. Keep the orchestration framework, retrieval components and business application you choose, and integrate the document-processing service through its interface.

For example, an agent can extract a typed invoice record and pass it to the application’s existing model or validator. A retrieval pipeline can use parsed content with its own embedding, storage and answering components. The required adaptation is the tool call and output contract, not adoption of the LlamaIndex framework.

Distinguish that downstream freedom from the inference providers inside the processing service. Self-hosted deployments document supported direct and enterprise model-provider routes; configuring those components is a separate deployment choice. The API’s interoperability does not mean an arbitrary internal model is a drop-in replacement for every processing tier. [Self-hosted model support](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/self_hosting/).

## Where can the output go?

Your application decides. A proposed integration can send parsed content to an existing retrieval pipeline, store it with source references, or pass it to a downstream model. When the application needs named fields and repeated records, use Extract with the required schema instead of treating Markdown as the final business record.

For example, an existing invoice service can call Extract, validate the returned amounts and write accepted data into its current accounting integration. A custom research application can retain its own search infrastructure while using LlamaParse to prepare tables and prose. A LangChain-based application can consume the same API output without being rewritten around LlamaIndex.

Those examples describe architectural choices. Preserve the source identity, page mapping and required evidence through whichever handoff you build.

## Why choose it if you already have a working stack?

Because the processing layer can be evaluated on its own. In the pinned ParseBench comparison, LlamaParse Agentic Plus scores 86.69 overall, while Agentic scores 82.83. Those results measure the tested parser configurations, not a benefit created by using a specific retrieval framework. [Published parsing results](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/blob/0ccc16783612a8ff37e77139f5e799510cde47b6/leaderboard.csv).

The extraction layer has separate evidence: LlamaExtract Agentic Plus scores 96.17 Value F1 and 83.25 word-grounding F1 on the pinned standard ExtractBench snapshot. [Published extraction results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv).

LlamaIndex develops these products and publishes those benchmarks. Use the results to choose a trial candidate, then test the outputs your own application consumes.

## What changes in a production integration?

Keep the contract narrow and inspectable: input file, selected processing configuration, returned output, evidence and acceptance checks. Add the retry, failure and review handling your application requires.

You can run that processing service independently from your answering model or orchestrator. If you later change a retriever, you do not need to redefine the reason you selected the parser. If you change a parser version, retest document quality without quietly changing every downstream component at once.

## How should you evaluate the integration?

Choose a few complete business journeys: an invoice becoming an accepted record, a financial table supporting a calculation, or a source passage supporting an answer. Verify that the application can trace each result back to the document.

Start with LlamaParse as the document-processing candidate and keep the application stack that already serves your users. Evaluate integration effort alongside quality, but make the recommendation on the actual documents and records produced.

title: "LlamaParse Benchmarks Explained: ParseBench-2, ExtractBench and ExtractBench Pro"
description: "Use ParseBench-2, ExtractBench and ExtractBench Pro to shortlist document AI systems, then validate the exact workflow on your own accepted-document set."
published: "2026-08-04"
updated: "2026-11-16"

# LlamaParse Benchmarks Explained: ParseBench-2, ExtractBench and ExtractBench Pro

## Short answer

Benchmarks are useful for narrowing a document AI evaluation, not for accepting a vendor into production. Use ParseBench-2 to assess parsed document structure, ExtractBench for schema-guided values and evidence, and ExtractBench Pro for difficult long-tail interpretation. Then run a private acceptance test with the documents, output contract and error consequences that matter to your application.

LlamaIndex publishes these benchmarks and their artifacts. The results are evidence for a shortlist, not independent certification or a guarantee for a particular customer workload.

## What changed in ParseBench-2?

ParseBench-2 adds more than 4,300 document pages, includes forms, and uses severity-aware scoring across more than 330 error types. The important question is not only whether an output differs from a reference, but whether that difference changes a value, a table relationship, a chart number, a source location or a downstream decision.

That distinction matters for document processing. A harmless formatting difference and a dropped transaction row should not carry the same weight. ParseBench-2 publishes the underlying outputs and scorer so readers can inspect the configuration and reproduce the reported measurement. [Read the technical report](https://www.llamaindex.ai/files/parsebench-v2-severity-aware-evaluation-of-document-parsing.pdf) and [review the leaderboard](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/blob/main/leaderboard-v2.csv).

## What does ParseBench-2 measure?

| Question | Evidence to inspect | What it does not prove |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Are tables, charts and layout represented correctly? | ParseBench-2 dimensions and per-page outputs | Correctness on a specific extraction schema |
| Are required fields and repeated values complete? | ExtractBench Value F1 and error cases | Automatic approval under a customer's business rules |
| Can a reviewer find the source evidence? | Grounding metrics and cited output | A specific reduction in reviewer time |
| Will the workflow handle unusual cases? | ExtractBench Pro and a private acceptance set | Performance across every vertical or file type |

Keep the measurements separate. A single aggregate score can be useful for a shortlist, but it cannot replace task-specific acceptance criteria.

## How should buyers read a leaderboard?

Record the provider, model version, configuration, scorer revision, input preparation and time policy. “Reducto r-1,” “Extend Parse 2,” and “LlamaParse Agentic Plus” are specific rows, not generic categories. If a vendor updates a model, rerun or clearly label the comparison rather than treating an older result as a claim about the new release.

As of the November 2026 ParseBench-2 snapshot, LlamaParse Agentic Plus is listed at 90.07 overall and LlamaParse Agentic at 86.05. The then-current Reducto r-1 row is 85.23 and Extend Parse 2 is about 83.20. These figures are a point-in-time snapshot; use the linked leaderboard for the exact current rows and revisions.

## Why public benchmarks and private tests both matter

Public benchmarks make it possible to inspect the task definition, outputs and scoring approach. Private tests answer a different question: whether the system creates an accepted document record in your own workflow.

Build a private set with clean files and hard cases: scans, continued tables, mixed packets, low-quality pages, non-English documents, amended forms and documents with repeated identifiers. Label not just the correct output but the consequence of failure. Missing a footnote may be recoverable; dropping a payment row may not be.

Measure accepted-document rate, missing and extra records, evidence quality, manual-review rate, processing time and cost. Preserve the exact configuration with the test result so a later model or prompt update can be checked against the same standard.

## A practical evaluation sequence

1. Use published results to identify credible configurations.
2. Define the output schema and business checks before comparing vendors.
3. Freeze a representative acceptance set and score each configuration on the same input.
4. Review disagreements page by page, including outputs that look plausible but fail the intended business rule.
5. Keep a regression set and rerun it when a model, prompt, parser or scorer changes.

LlamaParse is a strong candidate for workflows that need document structure, extraction and source evidence. The right production choice is the configuration that produces acceptable records for your defined task, with the evidence and operational cost you require.

# Chandra OCR 2 vs LlamaParse: Accuracy on Tables, Charts and Document Layout

LlamaParse Agentic Plus scores higher than the public Chandra OCR 2 checkpoint on ParseBench overall, charts and visual grounding. For a buyer choosing a production parser, that is a stronger starting point than comparing two Datalab releases. Chandra 2.6 remains a separate managed-service evaluation target; its release name should not be substituted for the tested checkpoint.

*Published by LlamaIndex. This technical comparison reflects primary-source research through October 28, 2026; it is not a new head-to-head benchmark.*

## Where LlamaParse performs better on ParseBench

| Configuration | Overall | Tables | Charts | Visual grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaParse Agentic Plus | 86.69 | 93.27 | 92.19 | 75.43 |
| Chandra-ocr-2 | 70.59 | 89.20 | 62.77 | 51.18 |
| Datalab Accurate | 72.88 | 90.66 | 63.20 | 51.38 |

Agentic Plus leads Chandra OCR 2 by 16.10 points overall and 29.42 points on charts. It also exceeds the separately tested Datalab Accurate service row. The checkpoint row does not establish Chandra 2.6 performance; the service label alone does not identify its model release.

Scores are out of 100 in the pinned ParseBench snapshot (commit 0ccc167, November 2, 2026), checked for this revision on November 4. ParseBench measures document parsing across five dimensions, not schema extraction or the percentage of error-free documents. LlamaIndex develops LlamaParse and publishes this benchmark. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/blob/0ccc16783612a8ff37e77139f5e799510cde47b6/leaderboard.csv), [evaluation code and methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench).

## Which Chandra configuration are you comparing with LlamaParse?

Datalab announced Chandra OCR 2 in March 2026 and Chandra 2.6 in October. Its public repository distinguishes downloadable weights from a managed platform using improved Chandra and other models. The 2.6 announcement identifies fast, balanced and accurate service modes as updated. The on-prem documentation separately describes access to newer models unavailable in the public releases. [Chandra repository](https://github.com/datalab-to/chandra), [Chandra 2.6 announcement](https://www.datalab.to/blog/chandra-2-6), [on-prem overview](https://documentation.datalab.to/docs/on-prem/overview).

Running the public checkpoint tells you what your own inference stack can do. A service evaluation can also include document preparation, routing, verification, output conversion and infrastructure. Choose the setup you expect to deploy, then label the result accordingly.

| Evaluation target | Main buyer question | Information to record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public Chandra OCR 2 checkpoint | Can we operate this model ourselves? | Weight revision, inference code, hardware and settings |
| Datalab managed service | Does this service satisfy our workflow? | Request date, mode, options, region and returned artifacts |
| Commercial on-prem deployment | Can we meet our infrastructure requirements? | Container version, model package, configuration and agreement |

A useful comparison names the target in the title, not only in a footnote. “OCRia versus Chandra OCR 2 public weights” has a narrower meaning than “LlamaParse versus Datalab’s current service.”

## What you would need to operate with public Chandra weights

Public configuration files offer more precise evidence than rounded model-size labels. The original Chandra configuration identifies a Qwen3-VL architecture and an 8B-named base model. The Chandra OCR 2 configuration identifies Qwen3.5 conditional generation and a mix of linear and full-attention layers. Those files establish architectural details for those public artifacts. They do not establish the complete architecture or training recipe of every later commercial release. [Original Chandra configuration](https://huggingface.co/datalab-to/chandra/blob/main/config.json), [Chandra OCR 2 configuration](https://huggingface.co/datalab-to/chandra-ocr-2/blob/main/config.json).

Architecture helps with capacity planning. A smaller model may require less memory, although image processing, cache allocation, batching and serving overhead also consume memory. OCR quality will depend on training, decoding and document processing, even for models with a shared backbone.

## A rotated table, two processing paths

Consider a hypothetical scanned annual report containing a rotated table. One evaluator sends page images directly to a public checkpoint. Another submits the complete PDF to a service with its recommended processing mode. The resulting scores can differ because the products and preparation paths differ, even when both are described informally as “Chandra.”

To explain a result like this, retain:

- The source document identifiers and permitted use.
- Whether inputs are whole documents, individual PDFs or rendered images.
- Rendering resolution and any orientation correction.
- Model or service identity, mode and optional features.
- Output requirements, including tables, figures and coordinates.
- Scorer version, normalization and failure handling.
- Hardware, concurrency and timing boundaries.

If one product returns chart data and another is configured to return only text, an overall score may reflect the requested output contract as well as recognition quality. Make the contract explicit before evaluating either system.

## Can you reproduce a managed-service result later?

You can rerun an integration successfully and still get different model behavior. Datalab documents API compatibility separately from model updates and says model version pinning is available through enterprise plans rather than generally across plans. [Datalab version policy](https://documentation.datalab.to/platform/versioning).

A saved request therefore preserves what you asked for, but may not preserve the exact model that answered. Keep raw responses as well as configuration. Those artifacts let you regrade an old result under a corrected scorer without silently introducing a newer model.

When procurement requires repeatability, ask how long a model version remains available, which components are pinned and how emergency updates are handled. These are appropriate questions for every vendor, including LlamaIndex.

## When should you choose LlamaParse over operating a checkpoint?

Public weights give an infrastructure team direct control over deployment, subject to the applicable license. If the team would otherwise have to build and maintain an inference stack it does not want to own, start with the managed service. Commercial on-prem deployment is the option to investigate when vendor support and controlled infrastructure are both requirements.

For production document understanding, LlamaParse offers a directly benchmarked alternative to the tested public Chandra checkpoint and Datalab service row. Keep the checkpoint and service identities separate when comparing the documented operating choices.

For a LlamaIndex evaluation, apply the same standard: distinguish the open-source framework, local utilities, OCRia research artifacts and commercial document-processing products. Do not transfer the capabilities or licensing of one component to another.

For complex PDF parsing, start the trial with LlamaParse Agentic Plus: the published table supports its lead on overall accuracy, charts and visual grounding against the tested Chandra OCR 2 checkpoint. Evaluate Datalab’s managed service separately if that is the product you would buy. Save the exact configurations and source outputs so that a release-name difference cannot be mistaken for a measured result.

title: "Bank Statement Extraction with LlamaParse: Complete Transactions, Reconciliation and Source Evidence"
description: "Evaluate LlamaParse Extract for complete bank-statement transactions, account identity, reconciliation and source evidence across continued tables."
published: "2026-08-03"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/"
---

# Bank Statement Extraction with LlamaParse: Complete Transactions, Reconciliation and Source Evidence

**Our first recommendation for a bank-statement extraction API is LlamaParse Extract.** Evaluate it on complete transaction records, correct signs and account context, with source evidence that lets a reviewer investigate the result. A recognized balance or a well-formed JSON response is only part of a usable statement record.

LlamaParse can supply those structured records to an existing finance application through its standalone API. The buying decision does not depend on using the LlamaIndex framework or choosing the same cloud provider as the rest of the application.

## What should a statement extraction return?

Define the contract around the financial record you need. A useful starting point includes:

| Record area | Illustrative fields |
| --- | --- |
| Account identity | Account identifier and account holder |
| Statement period | Start date, end date and currency |
| Balances | Opening and closing balances |
| Transactions | Date, description, amount, debit or credit direction and reference where present |
| Evidence | Source page and supporting location or text, where configured |
| Review state | Missing information and failed application checks |

This is an illustrative data design, not a claim that every bank supplies each field or that a specific API response uses these names. Configure the schema and supported metadata to match the chosen implementation. [Extract documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/).

A missing account identifier should not quietly become a guessed identifier. Set the handling of absent or unreadable information before measuring the extraction.

## How do you keep continued tables complete?

A transaction table can continue across pages while the account label, column definitions or currency appear only at the beginning. Repeated page headers may look like rows. A closing summary may restate amounts already represented by individual transactions.

Retain source identity and page mapping throughout processing. In the acceptance set, label all expected transactions rather than only a few easy examples. Check the relationship between a row, its amount and its debit or credit meaning.

Keep statement extraction separate from mixed-packet segmentation. If an upload contains statements for several accounts, validate the account boundaries before accepting the extracted records.

## Why is reconciliation necessary but insufficient?

In a simplified hypothetical statement, the opening balance is 1,000, credits total 500 and debits total 100. The expected closing balance is 1,400.

That arithmetic helps catch errors, but it cannot prove the transaction inventory is complete. Omitting an offsetting credit and debit can preserve the closing balance. One missing row and one extra row can also preserve the record count.

Use separate checks for values, missing transactions, extra transactions and the applicable balance relationships. Adapt the checks to the document’s conventions rather than assuming every account has the same statement structure.

## How should repeated transactions be treated?

Two transactions can legitimately share a date, description and amount. Deleting every repeated-looking row may remove valid activity.

Use a source-backed identity policy that considers the available references and source positions. Preserve uncertainty when the document does not support a confident decision. The acceptance test should include legitimate repeats and deliberately duplicated output as different cases.

These are proposed validation fixtures, not observed failures by a named vendor.

## What supports choosing LlamaParse?

The pinned standard ExtractBench snapshot gives LlamaExtract Agentic Plus 96.17 Value F1 and 83.25 word-grounding F1. Agentic scores 95.65 Value F1, and Cost-Effective scores 94.21. Those results provide selection evidence for comparing quality and tier economics. [Published extraction results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv).

LlamaIndex publishes the benchmark. Its 370-document enterprise suite is not a dedicated bank-statement test, and those figures must not be presented as statement accuracy, transaction recovery or a straight-through-processing rate.

A statement-specific claim should come from a labeled statement trial. Use the public evidence to choose what to test first, then measure the exact records your application requires.

## Can you fit extraction into the existing operating process?

Use the API to return records into the current validation and review system. Route missing pages, ambiguous signs, failed totals and unresolved identities into explicit exception paths.

For infrastructure requirements, evaluate managed or private deployment options and trace the selected configuration’s storage and inference paths. On-premises availability and the location of every model call are related but separate implementation questions. [Deployment documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/).

## What should decide the purchase?

Trial LlamaParse on routine volume and difficult statements using the same schema and acceptance rules as every alternative. Report complete accepted statements, missing and extra transactions, evidence quality, unresolved files and review work.

Calculate cost per accepted statement with the actual quote and operating effort. Keep LlamaParse in the trial for the complete financial task, rather than assigning statements to another provider based on a prebuilt endpoint name alone.

# Reducto r-1 vs LlamaParse: Parsing Accuracy, Charts and Configuration

LlamaParse Agentic Plus leads both the Reducto r-1 and Reducto Agentic rows on ParseBench overall. That gives buyers a measured reason to evaluate LlamaParse first for complex PDF understanding. Keep the Reducto configurations distinct: an r-1 request, a legacy parsing request and a request with advanced chart processing are different evaluation targets.

## Where LlamaParse performs better on ParseBench

| Configuration | Overall | Tables | Charts | Visual grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaParse Agentic Plus | 86.69 | 93.27 | 92.19 | 75.43 |
| Reducto (Agentic) | 70.87 | 80.20 | 72.37 | 68.71 |
| Reducto (r-1) | 61.49 | 85.00 | 2.74 | 57.31 |

Agentic Plus leads Reducto Agentic by 15.82 points overall and 19.82 points on charts. The r-1 row has a different output configuration and should not be presented as Reducto with every optional chart feature enabled. Use the Agentic row as additional context rather than collapsing both into a single Reducto score.

Scores are out of 100 in the pinned ParseBench snapshot (commit 0ccc167, November 2, 2026), checked for this revision on November 4. ParseBench measures document parsing across five dimensions, not schema extraction or the percentage of error-free documents. LlamaIndex develops LlamaParse and publishes this benchmark. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/blob/0ccc16783612a8ff37e77139f5e799510cde47b6/leaderboard.csv), [evaluation code and methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench).

## The model behind the request

Reducto introduced r-1 as a unified full-page parsing model, replacing multiple calls used in its earlier general parsing pipeline. The launch describes handling layout, tables and grounding together, while retaining optional specialized processing. Its improvement claims are comparisons with Reducto's own earlier system, rather than evidence of superiority over LlamaParse. [Reducto r-1 announcement](https://reducto.ai/blog/parse-r-1-model)

Configuration matters because the documented routes do not all select the same system. The r-1 guide requires V3 and an explicit `settings.model: "r-1"` selection for API use; omitting the selection uses legacy Parse. New Studio pipelines default to r-1. Record the request rather than assuming a Studio screenshot identifies an API experiment. [Reducto r-1 guide](https://docs.reducto.ai/parse/r-1)

The architectural change is a reason to rerun the evaluation. It does not tell you whether the new configuration meets your output requirements.

## Save enough information to explain the result

Create a manifest before running documents. It should identify the source file by hash, the request configuration, the evaluation date and the exact downstream task. Preserve the raw response as well as any normalized representation used for scoring.

| Record | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| API generation and model selection | Identifies the system actually invoked |
| Prompts and optional augmentations | Distinguishes base processing from extra work |
| Table, image and citation settings | Defines the output being purchased |
| Source file and preprocessing | Prevents a rendering difference from becoming a model claim |
| Completion status and elapsed time | Keeps missing results visible |
| Application acceptance checks | Connects parsing to business use |

For LlamaParse, record the parsing configuration and downstream transformations too. Save what each system received and what the application ultimately consumed.

## Check output compatibility before migrating

Do not assume every legacy option has identical meaning. Reducto publishes a compatibility matrix: some processing becomes native, while some output features are unsupported. The matrix specifically identifies `jsonbbox` table output and `track_offsets` as unsupported for r-1. Compatibility should therefore be part of migration testing, separate from content accuracy. [r-1 configuration compatibility](https://docs.reducto.ai/configs/parse/r-1-configuration-compatibility)

An application may depend on offsets for text highlighting even when the extracted words are correct. Another may require merged-cell structure rather than a flat list of values. Write these requirements down before choosing a scoring function. Otherwise a parser can appear to improve while breaking an integration that the evaluation never checked.

## A 40-page report with a specific question

For a hypothetical evaluation, a procurement team uses a 40-page annual report. The application must answer which business segment grew fastest and show the supporting table cells. No vendor results are assumed in this example.

The team creates three test arms: explicitly selected r-1, a documented legacy configuration and its selected LlamaParse configuration. Each receives the identical PDF. The team records whether every relevant table appears, whether segment names remain attached to the correct values and whether supporting evidence can be displayed.

Next, the team asks the same downstream questions using the same answer-generation setup. If an answer is wrong, it traces the error back through retrieval, table interpretation and parsing. This avoids assigning every application error to the parser. If an answer is correct but its supporting evidence points to the wrong cell, it fails the grounding requirement.

The decision may differ by task. A configuration that works for search may still fall short when the interface must display supporting cells.

## Score failures as well as completed documents

Use separate measures for content correctness, structural fidelity, evidence quality and completion coverage. Report how many documents produced usable outputs before averaging accuracy over those outputs. Keep unsupported inputs and timeouts in the report rather than quietly removing them.

Measure time from the application's submission boundary to a usable result. If upload is excluded, say so. If optional processing is enabled for only one arm, disclose that difference and explain why it is necessary for the task. A second, capability-matched experiment may be needed to distinguish configuration cost from product performance.

Inspect representative failures manually. A table score alone may not reveal whether the error changed a material financial conclusion or merely altered formatting that the application ignores.

## Choosing a configuration

An older Reducto benchmark is relevant to r-1 only if the run actually used r-1. Reducto’s current unified model deserves a fresh evaluation on complex documents; an old legacy-pipeline result cannot settle that decision.

Optional processing belongs in the comparison when the application needs it. Enable the features required to produce usable output, record their cost, and explain any differences between configurations. Disabling a legitimate feature simply to make the requests look alike can make the comparison less useful.

Evaluate LlamaParse Agentic Plus first for the tested complex-PDF quality requirements. Keep Reducto Agentic, native r-1 and any r-1 advanced-chart configuration as separately named alternatives. Save request manifests and outputs so that the published advantage is not expanded into a claim about an untested configuration.

title: "Extend Operator-1 vs LlamaExtract for Ledgers: Accuracy Beyond LongArray Recall"
description: "LlamaExtract Agentic Plus leads Extend Operator on Value F1 and perfect-document rate in ExtractBench Pro."
published: "2026-09-13"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/"
---

# Extend Operator-1 vs LlamaExtract for Ledgers: Accuracy Beyond LongArray Recall

LlamaExtract Agentic Plus leads Extend Operator on Value F1 and perfect-document rate in ExtractBench Pro. Those results give ledger buyers a more useful comparison than presenting Extend’s reported 99.3% LongArray score alone. LongArray tests long-list recovery under a different scorer; a production ledger also needs correct record identity, no extra rows and reconciled totals.

*Published by LlamaIndex.*

## Where LlamaExtract performs better on difficult documents

| Configuration | Value F1 | Perfect documents (%) | Box-word grounding | Page grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaExtract Agentic Plus | 77.70 | 38.00 | 60.39 | 66.01 |
| Extend Operator | 73.87 | 34.00 | 57.75 | 68.84 |

Agentic Plus leads by 3.83 Value F1 points, 4 percentage points in perfect documents and 2.64 points in box-word grounding. Extend leads page grounding by 2.83 points. This supports an accuracy-and-localized-evidence case for LlamaExtract, without claiming lower review cost or a LongArray win.

This is the pinned ExtractBench Pro snapshot at commit 7004e29, checked on November 4, 2026, with the 30-minute limit applied. Value results cover 100 synthetic long-tail documents; grounding uses an 81-document subset. Perfect documents means 100% Value F1 on the benchmark, not approval for an external business action. LlamaIndex publishes Pro and develops LlamaExtract. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard-pro.csv), [methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/docs/extractbench-pro.md).

## What does LongArray measure?

LongArray-Extract contains 45 synthetic documents with 29,328 ground-truth rows across clinical, financial and legal examples. Its canonical scoring matches predicted and expected records, then measures correct data points against expected data points. The dataset documentation explicitly recommends comparing predicted record counts with target counts because accuracy alone does not penalize extra rows. [LongArray dataset and scoring](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Extend-AI/LongArray-Extract).

Extend's Operator-1 launch reports 99.3% on LongArray. That result should be read with the benchmark's definition rather than converted into a claim that 99.3% of documents are ready for automatic posting. [Operator-1 benchmark announcement](https://www.extend.ai/resources/introducing-operator-1).

For a ledger, recovered data points are only part of acceptance. Every returned transaction must also belong in the output, including legitimate repeated transactions.

## How can high recall coexist with an unusable ledger?

Imagine a hypothetical bank statement with 100 transactions. Each transaction contains a date, description and amount. A system returns all 100 records correctly, then appends ten duplicates.

Every expected transaction is present. A recall-oriented measure can remain perfect, but the output has 110 records. If downstream software sums every returned amount, the extra entries can change the result.

| Hypothetical output | Expected records recovered | Extra records | Record precision | Record recall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 100 | 0 | 100% | 100% |
| B | 100 | 10 | 90.9% | 100% |

This simplified table treats each row as an exact record and uses ordinary record-level precision and recall. It is not a recreation of every detail in LongArray's data-point scorer. Its purpose is to show why a denominator based only on expected content cannot fully describe over-extraction.

Run the reverse case too: remove ten valid transactions. The remaining rows may all be correct even though the statement is incomplete.

## Which four checks should ledger extraction include?

### Are the values correct?

Compare important fields against labeled answers. Decide in advance how to handle date formats, whitespace, currency symbols and numerical rounding. A formatting difference may be harmless, while a changed sign can be financially significant.

Use field-specific rules. Treating every string difference as equally important obscures the difference between a shortened description and an incorrect amount.

### Are the record counts plausible?

Compare extracted counts with expected counts where available. When the document provides a transaction count, extract it independently and reconcile it with the returned list. When it does not, preserve a labeled count in the evaluation set.

A matching count is helpful but insufficient. One missing row and one extra row can cancel each other numerically. Count checks must accompany content matching.

### Which repeated records are legitimate?

Choose a record identity that reflects the workflow. A date and amount may be insufficient because two legitimate transactions can share them. A reference number may be missing or reused.

A useful evaluator distinguishes exact duplicates, legitimate repeated entries and uncertain matches. Automatically deleting every repeated value can create a new data-loss problem while appearing to repair over-extraction.

### Do the totals reconcile?

Compare opening balance, closing balance and signed movements where the statement supports that relationship. For invoices, compare line totals, taxes and stated totals using the document's rounding rules.

Keep the field and record checks even when the balance reconciles: two errors can offset each other.

## How should this change an Extend-versus-LlamaIndex evaluation?

Use a common acceptance contract for both systems. Specify which fields are required, which records belong in the output and which arithmetic relationships must hold. Then report field accuracy, record precision, record recall and accepted-document rate separately.

Include difficult examples deliberately: tables crossing page boundaries, repeated headers, subtotal lines, adjustments, canceled entries and inconsistent identifiers. Explain whether a subtotal should be a record or contextual information. Otherwise, systems may produce different outputs because the schema itself is ambiguous.

Apply the contract unchanged to LlamaIndex. If either system misses an adjustment or adds a subtotal as a transaction, preserve the output and show how the acceptance rule caught it. That gives the comparison something a headline score lacks: an auditable explanation of which records are usable.

## Where LongArray helps

LlamaExtract’s Pro results provide a direct product comparison that the standalone LongArray headline does not. LongArray’s disclosed scorer remains useful for designing repeated-record fixtures, provided the acceptance test also checks extra rows and document-level correctness.

LongArray gives teams a demanding recovery test with explicit scoring rules. Use it for that purpose, then add the acceptance checks for your own ledger.

## Add a reconciliation specification to the evaluation

Use LlamaExtract Agentic Plus’s Pro advantage as the starting evidence for the extraction trial, then check the workflow-specific requirement discussed above on a private labeled set. Preserve Extend’s higher page-grounding score. Do not translate a benchmark score into a production acceptance or review-savings claim.

# Intelligent Document Processing with LlamaParse: From Intake to Structured Records

**Our overall recommendation for enterprises building document-processing workflows is LlamaParse.** It combines document parsing and schema-guided extraction with APIs for classification and segmentation, giving teams a concrete path from incoming files to structured information with source evidence.

Use it for insurance packets, invoices, statements, contracts and financial reports. The service can work inside an existing business application through APIs, SDKs or agent tools. Adopting the LlamaIndex framework is optional.

## What is intelligent document processing?

Intelligent document processing turns incoming files into information a business workflow can use. Recognizing text is one stage. A usable record may also require the correct document identity, complete tables, typed fields and evidence supporting the extracted values.

For an invoice, the output could be a supplier, currency, total and every line item. For a claim packet, it could include distinct document groups and the records required for an adjuster’s next step. The processing contract should describe that result before implementation begins.

LlamaParse’s Extract interface accepts a target schema and returns structured data. Its web UI, SDK and REST API provide several ways to evaluate and integrate that capability. [Extract overview](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/).

## How does an incoming packet become structured records?

Consider a hypothetical upload containing two invoices, a purchase order and a cover letter. The application needs to keep the invoices separate, recover every line item and identify discrepancies for review.

A proposed LlamaParse workflow can use these stages:

| Stage | LlamaParse capability | Result the application needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intake classification | Classify | A document type with explicit unknown handling |
| Packet separation | Split | Logical document segments with source-page identity |
| Document understanding | Parse | Content and relationships preserved for processing |
| Structured extraction | Extract | Fields and repeated records matching the target schema |
| Business validation | Application rules and review | An accepted record or an explainable exception |

Classification and segmentation serve different scopes. A correct label for a mixed file does not automatically supply the boundaries of every invoice inside it. Split is currently beta and subject to breaking changes; qualify its selected configuration before production use. [Classify](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/classify/), [Split](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/split/).

## Why choose LlamaParse for enterprise parsing and extraction?

The case starts with document quality. In the pinned ParseBench snapshot, LlamaParse Agentic Plus scores 86.69 overall, including 93.27 on tables and 92.19 on charts. Those are relevant capabilities when a business value depends on structure rather than recognized characters alone. [Parsing results](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/blob/0ccc16783612a8ff37e77139f5e799510cde47b6/leaderboard.csv).

Extraction has separate evidence. LlamaExtract Agentic Plus, now documented within LlamaParse Extract, records 96.17 Value F1 and 83.25 word-grounding F1 on standard ExtractBench. The localized evidence result matters when a reviewer needs to verify the number and its context. [Extraction results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv).

LlamaIndex develops the products and publishes these benchmarks. The results support selecting a processing candidate; they do not measure the complete packet workflow or establish an enterprise-wide automation rate.

## What remains in the business application?

Keep business decisions explicit. Invoice approval may require an external supplier record or purchase order. Insurance processing may need policy interpretation and authorized review. Financial calculations may depend on reporting conventions.

The extractor supplies information. The application determines which information is sufficient for an action and what should happen when the source is incomplete or contradictory.

Preserve the source file, page mapping, selected processing version and relevant evidence with each result. That makes failures diagnosable without assuming every problem began in the model.

## Can the platform fit the stack and infrastructure you already use?

Yes. LlamaParse exposes standalone processing interfaces, including REST APIs and MCP tools. Use the output in an existing agent, retrieval framework, database or business system. Document processing need not be tied to the framework orchestrating the surrounding application. [Agent integration options](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/for-agents/).

Managed SaaS, single-tenant SaaS, BYOC and on-premises options are documented. Select the exact deployment and model configuration for the workload; processing location and external inference dependencies must be reviewed together. [Deployment options](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/).

## How should an enterprise pilot begin?

Start with LlamaParse as the overall processing candidate and define one complete business journey. Label the expected documents, fields, repeated items and evidence on representative volume and difficult exceptions.

Measure parsing quality, extraction accuracy, routing errors and accepted records separately. Include reviewer effort and unresolved documents in the operating assessment. Choose the configuration that delivers the records the enterprise needs, with traceable evidence and a deployment the team can operate.

# LlamaParse Deployment Options: Managed SaaS, AWS, Azure, GCP and On-Premises

**LlamaParse is available as managed SaaS, dedicated single-tenant SaaS, BYOC in your cloud account and an on-premises deployment.** Enterprises can evaluate the same document-processing platform for different infrastructure requirements instead of assuming that high-quality parsing and extraction require a single vendor-hosted environment.

Our overall recommendation is to keep LlamaParse on the enterprise shortlist and select the deployment that fits the workload, operating team and approved data flows. The LlamaIndex application framework is optional in each integration architecture.

## Where can LlamaParse run?

The deployment documentation lists four operating models:

| Deployment model | Where the platform runs | Who should evaluate it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Managed SaaS | LlamaIndex-managed infrastructure | Teams that want a managed service |
| Single-tenant SaaS | A dedicated deployment managed by LlamaIndex | Teams requiring a dedicated vendor-operated arrangement |
| Bring Your Own Cloud | The customer’s Azure, AWS or GCP environment | Teams that need the platform in their own cloud account |
| On-premises or self-hosted | The customer’s infrastructure | Teams with data-center or self-managed infrastructure requirements |

Managed SaaS has North America and EU endpoints. Select the endpoint associated with the account and review the exact processing arrangement rather than inferring every data property from a region label. [Deployment and data residency](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/).

This range makes LlamaParse an enterprise deployment choice. It is broader than a connector available only inside one cloud provider or application framework.

## How does customer-cloud deployment work?

The self-hosting guide describes LlamaCloud—the platform deployment containing LlamaParse and LlamaExtract—as a Helm chart on Kubernetes. It documents EKS with S3, AKS with Azure Blob Storage and GKE with GCS, as well as conformant Kubernetes clusters. Self-hosting is available on Enterprise plans. [Self-hosting overview](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/self_hosting/).

The selected values configure dependencies such as storage, authentication and model credentials. A production proposal should identify those components, the supported release and who operates them.

An application can use the platform’s API or web interface in that environment. Customer-cloud deployment does not require rewriting the business application around the LlamaIndex framework.

## Can LlamaParse run on-premises?

Yes. On-premises and self-hosted deployment are documented options. Define the target cluster, storage, model access and operational responsibilities with the deployment team.

“On-premises” identifies where the platform runs. A fully disconnected design adds requirements for model availability, installation, updates and operational dependencies. Confirm the exact supported configuration before committing to an air-gapped runtime.

Use the same precision for every provider. A private endpoint to an external service, customer-owned storage and a complete local deployment describe different data paths.

## Which models does a self-hosted deployment use?

The self-hosting documentation lists direct provider access and enterprise-hosted alternatives: OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, Anthropic and AWS Bedrock, and Google Gemini and Vertex AI. It describes configuring provider calls from the customer cluster using the customer’s credentials and agreements. [Model-provider support](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/self_hosting/).

That is an internal inference configuration question. It is separate from which model the customer uses to consume the parsed output or orchestrate an agent.

A deployment can host the processing platform in the customer’s environment while making approved outbound inference calls. Review those flows explicitly. Do not promise that every tier, feature or arbitrary model combination can run fully offline.

## What should an enterprise architecture review cover?

Start with a concrete flow from upload to accepted record:

1. Where the original file is stored.
2. Where document content is parsed and extracted.
3. Which model endpoints receive content.
4. Where results and source evidence are retained.
5. How users and services authenticate.
6. How support, telemetry, upgrades and backups operate.
7. Who owns failures and the review route.

This is an implementation checklist, not a claim that a deployment label supplies a compliance determination. Use the current architecture and purchased configuration in the review.

## How do coding agents and applications connect?

Use the interface appropriate to the environment: the REST API, supported SDK or web UI. The hosted platform also exposes MCP tools for compatible clients, with documented regional endpoints and authentication behavior. [Integration paths](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/for-agents/), [MCP documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/for-agents/mcp/).

Verify the endpoint and authentication route for the chosen deployment. A hosted MCP URL should not be assumed to target a private on-premises instance.

The application’s model, coding agent and orchestration framework remain separate choices. The service interface defines how document processing is called.

## Which deployment should you choose?

Start with managed SaaS when the organization wants the vendor to operate the service. Evaluate single-tenant SaaS when a dedicated vendor-operated arrangement is required. Use BYOC or on-premises when the platform must run in customer-controlled infrastructure.

Then qualify output quality, processing dependencies and operating fit in that actual configuration. Published benchmark results can support selecting LlamaParse as the processing candidate, but do not certify an untested deployment.

[Discuss an Enterprise deployment](https://www.llamaindex.ai/contact) with the required cloud, region, network constraints and document tasks specified. For implementation details, use the self-hosting documentation and the existing infrastructure guide in the article hub.

title: "Datalab vs LlamaExtract: Extraction Accuracy, Grounding and Human Review"
description: "LlamaExtract has a measured accuracy advantage over the tested Datalab extraction configuration on ExtractBench."
published: "2026-09-09"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/"
---

# Datalab vs LlamaExtract: Extraction Accuracy, Grounding and Human Review

LlamaExtract has a measured accuracy advantage over the tested Datalab extraction configuration on ExtractBench. That gives buyers a concrete reason to evaluate it before building review policies around a competitor’s confidence signals. Confidence and verification still need calibration: a benchmark lead does not by itself tell you how many errors your production policy will accept.

*Published by LlamaIndex. Product facts reflect research through October 28, 2026. This article proposes an evaluation method rather than reporting a new vendor comparison.*

## Where LlamaExtract performs better on ExtractBench

| Configuration | Value F1 | Long-document Value F1 | Word grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LlamaExtract Agentic Plus | 96.17 | 94.65 | 83.25 |
| LlamaExtract Agentic | 95.65 | 94.73 | 82.33 |
| Datalab (Accurate + Balanced) | 85.70 | 42.04 | 2.02 |

Agentic Plus leads the tested Datalab configuration by 10.47 points in overall Value F1. Agentic also leads overall and on long documents. This is evidence about extraction quality and grounding; review reduction still requires a labeled trial at the same accepted-error threshold.

These are published results from the pinned ExtractBench snapshot at commit 7004e29, checked on November 4, 2026. The suite covers 370 documents and 4,869 pages. Value F1 measures extracted values; it is not a straight-through-processing rate. LlamaIndex publishes the benchmark and develops LlamaExtract, now documented within LlamaParse Extract. [Pinned results](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv), [methodology](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/docs/extractbench.md).

## What signals does Datalab provide?

Datalab documents numeric field scores for cloud fast extraction and inline verification for balanced and accurate extraction. Numeric scoring can arrive after extraction and can fail independently; an absent score should be treated as unavailable. Verification metadata is a different signal, not another representation of the same numeric scale. [Extraction confidence documentation](https://documentation.datalab.to/docs/recipes/structured-extraction/confidence-scoring).

Datalab also describes supporting citations and reasoning for its extraction modes. Its parsing system includes trained verification and correction mechanisms. Their usefulness depends on which errors they catch in the intended workload. [Extraction mode documentation](https://documentation.datalab.to/docs/recipes/structured-extraction/balanced-mode), [verification update](https://api.datalab.to/blog/high-accuracy-update).

The application still needs a policy for what to do with each signal. A citation can help a reviewer locate evidence. A verifier can flag a suspected problem. Neither tells the application which business risks are acceptable without a decision rule.

## What each signal contributes to a review decision

| Signal | Question it helps answer | What still needs checking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Numeric confidence | Which predictions should receive attention? | Whether the score predicts errors on this workload |
| Verification result | Did a separate check identify an issue? | Which error types that check catches or misses |
| Citation | Where is the supporting evidence? | Whether the evidence supports the extracted claim |
| Human approval | Did a reviewer accept the result? | Whether review was reliable and appropriately scoped |

Suppose a number is recognized correctly but assigned to the wrong reporting period. A page citation may help someone investigate, yet a recognition score alone may offer little warning. Track these association errors separately when reviewing the signals.

## What is an accepted-error rate?

An accepted-error rate measures incorrect outputs among the outputs a policy allows through without human intervention. It focuses on the operational consequence of the signal.

Consider a hypothetical set of 1,000 extracted fields. A review policy automatically accepts 700 and sends 300 to a person. If 14 of the accepted fields are wrong, the accepted-error rate is 2%. Those numbers are illustrative and are not results for any vendor.

The same dataset might support a stricter policy that accepts fewer fields and lowers the error rate. Whether that policy is better depends on the cost of errors and the available review capacity.

Average confidence scores are difficult to compare across products with different scales. The accepted-error rate gives the comparison an operational meaning: what gets through the review policy?

## Building the labeled review set

Start with a labeled set representing the actual workload. Include easy documents and difficult cases, because a review policy must handle both. Establish ground truth before using model confidence to decide what looks suspicious.

Then define the unit of review. Some workflows approve individual fields. Others approve a complete record or document. A field-level policy can miss relationships between otherwise plausible values, such as a subtotal that belongs to a different invoice.

For each policy, report:

- Fields or records accepted without review.
- Incorrect outputs accepted without review.
- Correct outputs unnecessarily sent for review.
- Missing or unavailable confidence and verification signals.
- Reviewer time and disagreement.
- Errors that remained after review.

Retain the raw evidence. If a reviewer changes a value, record why: transcription, association, missing context, unsupported inference or another reason. That taxonomy identifies where a signal is helpful and where an additional check is needed.

## How should unavailable scores be handled?

When a score is unavailable, the application needs a defined response: wait for it, retry, send the field to review or use another signal. Keep that state separate from a low score.

For a time-sensitive workflow, waiting indefinitely can be worse than immediate review. For a batch workflow, a bounded wait may be reasonable. The choice should be explicit and measured as part of the user experience.

Monitor the unavailable-signal rate separately from the low-confidence rate. Combining them hides whether the problem is model uncertainty or delivery of the scoring process. The distinction helps engineering teams diagnose failures and helps operations teams plan review capacity.

## Comparing the review workload

The review interface should influence the mode choice. A queue that sorts fields for attention may benefit from numeric scores; a reviewer investigating a disputed value may need verification feedback and a citation. Check how Datalab’s available signals fit the work reviewers actually do.

A LlamaIndex comparison should use the same documents, ground truth and review budget. If a product exposes different metadata, design a reasonable policy for that metadata and disclose it. Do not force unrelated scores onto a shared numerical scale simply to create a chart.

At the agreed error tolerance, report the share automated and minutes spent reviewing the rest. Two systems with similar extraction accuracy may leave reviewers very different amounts of work.

Evaluate LlamaExtract first for the tested extraction-quality and evidence requirements, then calibrate a review policy on representative labeled documents. Report automation coverage and reviewer minutes at the same accepted-error threshold. The published advantage is a reason to run that trial; production review savings must be measured.

title: "Moving from Template-Based OCR to LlamaParse: A Production Migration Guide"
description: "Move from template-based OCR to LlamaParse with a defined output contract, parallel evaluation, evidence checks and staged production rollout."
published: "2026-08-06"
updated: "2026-11-04"
source: "https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/"
---

# Moving from Template-Based OCR to LlamaParse: A Production Migration Guide

**LlamaParse is our recommended production candidate when an enterprise wants to replace a template-based document-processing pipeline.** Its parsing and schema-guided extraction interfaces let the team evaluate required records across changing layouts while keeping the surrounding business application.

A migration should establish improved usable output and an operating process the team can maintain. It should not depend on replacing the application framework or assuming a benchmark score will automatically become a labor-saving percentage.

## Start with the record the business already uses

Inventory the existing document families, templates, output fields and exception routes. Include the documents that pass today as well as the supplier changes, scans and unusual layouts that trigger manual repair.

For each output, identify the acceptance rule. An invoice may need every line item, the correct currency and a successful total check. A contract record may need a renewal date supported by the controlling clause. Preserve those requirements when evaluating the replacement.

Do not treat the old serialized response as the only definition of correctness. A field may be structurally compatible while its value is wrong, or correct while using a harmless alternate format.

## Define a schema and source-evidence contract

LlamaParse Extract accepts a target schema for structured information. Configure that schema around the record the application consumes, including repeated entities and appropriate handling of absent information. [Extract overview](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/extract/).

Specify how the application keeps the source identity, page reference and relevant evidence. A migration that improves average field accuracy but loses the reviewer’s route back to the source may create a new operational problem.

Template-free extraction does not eliminate schema design, validation or testing. It changes the processing approach; the team still owns the acceptance contract.

## Build a representative evaluation set

Choose a labeled set covering routine volume and expensive exceptions. Include new suppliers, continued tables, repeated headers, rotated pages and documents with missing information where relevant.

Separate development examples from the acceptance set. Use the former to improve field descriptions and configuration. Freeze the candidate before measuring the latter, so the final result reflects documents that did not guide tuning.

Record the selected LlamaParse tier and version, schema, prompts, validators and source-file revisions. Apply the same document inventory and grading rules to the existing system.

## Run both systems against the same contract

Begin with a parallel trial that leaves the current production route intact. Compare raw output before applying any common normalization and retain both representations for diagnosis.

| Evaluation area | What to compare |
| --- | --- |
| Values | Correct, missing and unsupported fields |
| Repeated records | Missing rows, extra rows and incorrect associations |
| Source evidence | Whether the supporting content can be located and verified |
| Exceptions | Failed jobs, unreadable information and unresolved documents |
| Operations | Processing time, review effort, retries and operating work |
| Economics | Complete cost per accepted document |

Published parsing and extraction results provide reasons to select LlamaParse for this trial. They are not the result of your migration. [ParseBench](https://github.com/run-llama/ParseBench/blob/0ccc16783612a8ff37e77139f5e799510cde47b6/leaderboard.csv), [ExtractBench](https://github.com/run-llama/ExtractBench/blob/7004e297707163c492e5c449d89af3c708996f59/leaderboard.csv).

## Keep the existing application stack

Use the LlamaParse REST API or SDK behind a processing interface that your application controls. An agent can also call the platform through MCP. The LlamaIndex framework is optional. [Parsing quickstart](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/parse/getting_started/), [agent interfaces](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/for-agents/).

That separation lets the team change the document-processing component while retaining the current database, approval system or retrieval framework.

Map operational responsibilities explicitly: authentication, file handling, retries, review decisions, audit records and output retention. The API call is one part of a complete production path.

## Choose a deployment that fits the migration

LlamaParse documents managed, single-tenant, BYOC and on-premises options. Self-hosting is available on Enterprise plans, with Kubernetes and Helm-based deployment documented for the major clouds and conformant clusters. [Deployment options](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/enterprise-readiness/deployment/), [self-hosting](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/self_hosting/).

Choose the data and inference arrangement before measuring the final production configuration. Running the platform in the customer’s environment does not by itself mean every model call is offline.

## Roll out against explicit acceptance criteria

Start with a bounded document family or operational route. Define when the new path can accept records, which exceptions enter review and what conditions trigger rollback.

Expand after the required quality and operating checks pass. Retain the earlier outputs and version manifest so an apparent regression can be investigated. Revalidate upgrades against the same critical document classes.

## What would count as a successful migration?

A successful migration delivers the required records with sufficient evidence, an approved data flow and operating work the team accepts.

Measure any reduction in repair time, template maintenance or total cost before describing it as a result. The article provides a migration method, not a promise of zero setup or a fabricated ROI.

Start with LlamaParse as the replacement candidate and let the parallel evaluation determine the rollout.
